# Build a Premium Lead Management System for Stampn Admin Panel

"""Admin console views for inbound "Get started" leads.

Any active admin may view the list and mark a lead contacted or delete it. The
public intake that creates these lives in ``console.public``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from django.utils import timezone
from drf_spectacular.utils import extend_schema
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.response import Response

from console import audit
from console.models import Lead
from console.permissions import AdminAPIView
from console.serializers_leads import LeadSerializer


class LeadListView(AdminAPIView):
    """GET /leads — every inbound lead, newest first."""

    @extend_schema(responses=LeadSerializer(many=True))
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        return Response(LeadSerializer(Lead.objects.all(), many=True).data)


class LeadDetailView(AdminAPIView):
    """PATCH /leads/{id} — toggle contacted status · DELETE /leads/{id}."""

    @extend_schema(request=None, responses=LeadSerializer)
    def patch(self, request: Request, lead_id: str) -> Response:
        lead = get_object_or_404(Lead, pk=lead_id)
        status = (request.data.get("status") or Lead.Status.CONTACTED).strip()
        if status not in Lead.Status.values:
            return Response(
                {"error": {"code": "INVALID_STATUS", "message": "Unknown lead status."}},
                status=400,
            )
        lead.status = status
        lead.contacted_at = timezone.now() if status == Lead.Status.CONTACTED else None
        lead.save(update_fields=["status", "contacted_at", "updated_at"])
        audit.record(
            request,
            "lead.update",
            target_type="lead",
            target_id=str(lead.id),
            metadata={"status": lead.status, "business_name": lead.business_name},
        )
        return Response(LeadSerializer(lead).data)

    @extend_schema(responses=None)
    def delete(self, request: Request, lead_id: str) -> Response:
        lead = get_object_or_404(Lead, pk=lead_id)
        audit.record(
            request,
            "lead.delete",
            target_type="lead",
            target_id=str(lead.id),
            metadata={"business_name": lead.business_name, "email": lead.email},
        )
        lead.delete()
        return Response(status=204)
=== SERIALIZERS ===
"""Serializers for inbound "Get started" leads.

``LeadCreateSerializer`` is what the *public* marketing form posts (with a
honeypot); ``LeadSerializer`` is the admin-facing read shape.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from rest_framework import serializers

from console.models import Lead


class LeadCreateSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    """Public write shape. ``botcheck`` is a honeypot — a real person leaves it
    empty; a bot that fills it is rejected quietly by the view."""

    botcheck = serializers.CharField(required=False, allow_blank=True, write_only=True)

    class Meta:
        model = Lead
        fields = ["name", "email", "phone", "business_name", "botcheck"]

    def create(self, validated_data):
        validated_data.pop("botcheck", None)
        return super().create(validated_data)


class LeadSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Lead
        fields = [
            "id",
            "name",
            "email",
            "phone",
            "business_name",
            "status",
            "contacted_at",
            "created_at",
        ]
        read_only_fields = fields

import { Loader2, Mail, Phone, Trash2, Check, RotateCcw } from 'lucide-react'
import { useLeads, useUpdateLead, useDeleteLead } from './api'
import Badge from '../../components/Badge'
import { fromNow } from '../../lib/format'

const STATUS_TONE = { new: 'info', contacted: 'success' }
const STATUS_LABEL = { new: 'New', contacted: 'Contacted' }

export default function LeadsHome() {
  const { data, isLoading } = useLeads()
  const rows = data ?? []
  const newCount = rows.filter((r) => r.status === 'new').length

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-5">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <h1 className="font-head text-2xl font-bold text-tx">Leads</h1>
        {newCount > 0 && <Badge tone="info">{newCount} new</Badge>}
      </div>
      <p className="-mt-3 text-sm text-tx-3">
        Inbound “Get started” requests from the marketing site.
      </p>

      {isLoading ? (
        <Loader2 className="mx-auto mt-6 animate-spin text-tx-3" />
      ) : (
        <List rows={rows} />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

function List({ rows }) {
  const update = useUpdateLead()
  const del = useDeleteLead()

  if (rows.length === 0) {
    return (
      <div className="rounded-card border border-line bg-surface p-8 text-center text-tx-3">
        No leads yet.
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="overflow-x-auto rounded-card border border-line bg-surface">
      <table className="w-full min-w-[720px] text-sm">
        <thead>
          <tr className="border-b border-line text-left text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-tx-3">
            <th className="px-4 py-3 font-semibold">Business</th>
            <th className="px-4 py-3 font-semibold">Contact</th>
            <th className="px-4 py-3 font-semibold">Status</th>
            <th className="px-4 py-3 font-semibold">Received</th>
            <th className="px-4 py-3 font-semibold text-right">Actions</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {rows.map((lead) => (
            <tr key={lead.id} className="border-b border-line last:border-0">
              <td className="px-4 py-3">
                <div className="font-semibold text-tx">{lead.business_name}</div>
              </td>
              <td className="px-4 py-3">
                <div className="text-tx">{lead.name}</div>
                <div className="mt-1 flex flex-col gap-0.5 text-xs text-tx-3">
                  <a
                    href={`mailto:${lead.email}`}
                    className="flex items-center gap-1 hover:text-brand"
                  >
                    <Mail size={12} /> {lead.email}
                  </a>
                  <a
                    href={`tel:${lead.phone}`}
                    className="flex items-center gap-1 hover:text-brand"
                  >
                    <Phone size={12} /> {lead.phone}
                  </a>
                </div>
              </td>
              <td className="px-4 py-3">
                <Badge tone={STATUS_TONE[lead.status]}>
                  {STATUS_LABEL[lead.status] ?? lead.status}
                </Badge>
              </td>
              <td className="px-4 py-3 text-tx-3">{fromNow(lead.created_at)}</td>
              <td className="px-4 py-3">
                <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
                  {lead.status === 'new' ? (
                    <button
                      onClick={() => update.mutate({ id: lead.id, status: 'contacted' })}
                      disabled={update.isPending}
                      className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-ctl border border-line px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-tx-2 hover:border-success hover:text-success disabled:opacity-60"
                    >
                      <Check size={14} /> Mark contacted
                    </button>
                  ) : (
                    <button
                      onClick={() => update.mutate({ id: lead.id, status: 'new' })}
                      disabled={update.isPending}
                      className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-ctl border border-line px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-tx-2 hover:border-brand hover:text-brand disabled:opacity-60"
                    >
                      <RotateCcw size={14} /> Reopen
                    </button>
                  )}
                  <button
                    onClick={() => {
                      if (window.confirm(`Delete lead from ${lead.business_name}?`)) {
                        del.mutate(lead.id)
                      }

                    disabled={del.isPending}
                    className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-ctl border border-line px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-tx-2 hover:border-danger hover:text-danger disabled:opacity-60"
                  >
                    <Trash2 size={14} />
                  </button>
                </div>
              </td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  )
}
=== API ===
import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import api from '../../lib/api'

export function useLeads() {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: ['leads'],
    queryFn: async () => (await api.get('/leads')).data,
  })
}

export function useUpdateLead() {
  const qc = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async ({ id, status }) => (await api.patch(`/leads/${id}`, { status })).data,
    onSuccess: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['leads'] }),
  })
}

export function useDeleteLead() {
  const qc = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (id) => (await api.delete(`/leads/${id}`)).data,
    onSuccess: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['leads'] }),
  })
}
```

    class Meta:

    def __str__(self) -> str:

    merchant's Support tab. Kept separate from ``Lead`` because a contact message
    is a support enquiry, not a sales lead.
    """

    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        NEW = "new", "New"
        READ = "read", "Read"
        REPLIED = "replied", "Replied"

## 22 · Claude

I've read the whole existing Leads slice. Here's where things stand before I write any code.

**The existing Leads feature is much smaller than the spec assumes.** `Lead` is six fields (name, email, phone, business_name, status, contacted_at) with exactly two statuses, one list view, one patch/delete view, and a 124-line table. What you've specced is a different product built on that name: ~40 lead fields, 24 statuses, activities, calls, a settings-driven dropdown system, scoring, import, dedup, and merchant conversion. That's roughly ten new models, thirty-odd endpoints, and a full frontend — weeks of work, not one session. I can build it, but not in one pass, and I don't want to dump 5,000 unreviewable lines on you and call it done. Your recent commits are staged (`stage 4`, `stage 5`), so I'd like to match that.

Three things in the spec genuinely conflict, and they change what I build:

**CRM Settings vs. business logic.** You want every dropdown to read from admin-managed settings "instead of hardcoded values." But other parts of the spec hardcode those same values: Lead Score is computed from Priority and Temperature, Convert-To-Merchant keys off `Converted`, and the KPI cards count `Interested`, `Demo Scheduled`, and `Customers` by name. If an admin renames or deletes a status, scoring and conversion silently break. The usual resolution is a fixed set of *system* statuses that logic depends on, with admin-configurable labels, colors, and ordering on top, plus freely-addable custom statuses that carry no logic.

**"Sales Users" don't exist yet.** `AdminRole` has SUPER_ADMIN, FINANCE, SUPPORT, MARKETING_ADMIN, ENGINEERING, READ_ONLY — no sales role. "Assigned Sales" and "Created By = Current Logged User" need a decision: add a `SALES` role to `AdminRole`, or treat any active admin as assignable.

**Convert-To-Merchant is the risky one.** Merchant + subscription + branch + admin-user provisioning already exists in `accounts/serializers.py` (signup). A second provisioning path that drifts from the first is how you end up with merchants that exist in one flow's shape but not the other's. It should call the same code, which likely means extracting it first.

<sub>Concern about the settings/logic conflict is design judgment, not something I verified against a spec you've ratified elsewhere — if you've already thought it through, say so and I'll build what you asked.</sub>

=== ENUMS ===
"""Platform-admin enums — admin roles + audit actions.

These are the *platform operator's* roles (Stampn staff), entirely separate from
the merchant-side ``core.enums.Role`` (a shop's staff). The full per-role
permission matrix arrives in Phase 12; Phase 1 only needs the role field + the
SUPER_ADMIN check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.db import models


class AdminRole(models.TextChoices):
    SUPER_ADMIN = "SUPER_ADMIN", "Super Admin"  # everything, incl. admin-team mgmt
    FINANCE = "FINANCE", "Finance"  # billing, refunds, plans, revenue
    SUPPORT = "SUPPORT", "Support"  # merchant support, impersonation, notes
    MARKETING_ADMIN = "MARKETING_ADMIN", "Marketing Admin"  # announcements, promos
    ENGINEERING = "ENGINEERING", "Engineering"  # ops, health, feature flags
    READ_ONLY = "READ_ONLY", "Read Only"  # view everything, change nothing
=== RBAC ===
"""Central RBAC permission matrix (Phase 12) — the single source of truth.

Every admin gate in the console derives from ``ROLE_PERMISSIONS`` here. The
per-domain permission classes in ``console.permissions`` (``IsFinanceAdmin``,
``IsSupportAdmin``, ``IsMarketingAdmin``) are thin lookups against this matrix,
so there is exactly one place that answers "which role may do what". Reads
(list/detail) stay open to any active admin (the ``IsAdminUser`` base) — the
matrix gates *mutations* and sensitive tools.

Super-admin implicitly holds every permission (see ``permissions_for``); the
other roles hold an explicit subset. ``READ_ONLY`` and (for now) ``ENGINEERING``
hold none — Engineering's ops permissions land with Phase 14.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from console.enums import AdminRole


class Permission:
    """Granular capability keys. Grouped by the phase that introduced the gate."""

    PLANS_MANAGE = "plans.manage"  # Phase 3 — create/edit/archive plans
    SUBSCRIPTIONS_MANAGE = "subscriptions.manage"  # Phase 4 — plan/status/comp/lock
    BILLING_MANAGE = "billing.manage"  # Phase 5 — retry/manual invoice/dunning
    REVENUE_VIEW = "revenue.view"  # Phase 7 — financial analytics
    SUPPORT_TOOLS = "support.tools"  # Phase 6 — impersonation, notes, account fixes
    MERCHANTS_MODERATE = "merchants.moderate"  # Phase 9 — flag queue / moderation
    MERCHANTS_SUSPEND = "merchants.suspend"  # Phase 9 — suspend/ban a merchant
    ANNOUNCEMENTS_MANAGE = "announcements.manage"  # Phase 10 — broadcasts
    PROMOTIONS_MANAGE = "promotions.manage"  # Phase 11 — coupons / promotions
    ADMINS_MANAGE = "admins.manage"  # Phase 12 — manage the admin team
    COMPLIANCE_EXPORT = "compliance.export"  # Phase 13 — export a merchant's data bundle (PII)
    COMPLIANCE_DELETE = "compliance.delete"  # Phase 13 — right-to-be-forgotten merchant delete
    RETENTION_MANAGE = "retention.manage"  # Phase 13 — edit the data-retention policy
    OPS_MANAGE = "ops.manage"  # Phase 14 — flags/settings/maintenance, job & webhook retries
    PARTNERS_MANAGE = "partners.manage"  # Phase E.1 — referral partners + reward config


ALL_PERMISSIONS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    value
    for name, value in vars(Permission).items()
    if not name.startswith("_") and isinstance(value, str)
)


# The matrix. Super-admin is intentionally absent here — it holds *everything*
# (resolved in ``permissions_for``) so a newly added permission is granted to
# super-admin by default and never silently withheld.
#
# The Phase 13 compliance keys (COMPLIANCE_EXPORT/DELETE, RETENTION_MANAGE) are
# deliberately in NO role's set below: they are super-admin-only. Merchant delete
# is irreversible and export dumps cross-tenant PII, so these stay the sharpest
# tools in the box — held only by the role that implicitly holds everything.
ROLE_PERMISSIONS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    AdminRole.FINANCE: frozenset(
        {
            Permission.PLANS_MANAGE,
            Permission.SUBSCRIPTIONS_MANAGE,
            Permission.BILLING_MANAGE,
            Permission.REVENUE_VIEW,
            Permission.PROMOTIONS_MANAGE,
            Permission.PARTNERS_MANAGE,
        }
    ),
    AdminRole.SUPPORT: frozenset(
        {
            Permission.SUPPORT_TOOLS,
            Permission.MERCHANTS_MODERATE,
        }
    ),
    AdminRole.MARKETING_ADMIN: frozenset({Permission.ANNOUNCEMENTS_MANAGE}),
    AdminRole.ENGINEERING: frozenset({Permission.OPS_MANAGE}),  # platform ops (Phase 14)
    AdminRole.READ_ONLY: frozenset(),  # view everything, mutate nothing
}


# Roles for which MFA is mandatory (flag per role — Phase 12 declares it, Phase 15
# enforces it at login). Any role holding a mutating permission is privileged.
MFA_REQUIRED_ROLES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        AdminRole.SUPER_ADMIN,
        AdminRole.FINANCE,
        AdminRole.SUPPORT,
        AdminRole.MARKETING_ADMIN,
        AdminRole.ENGINEERING,  # holds OPS_MANAGE since Phase 14 → now privileged
    }
)


def permissions_for(role: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Every permission a role holds (super-admin holds all)."""
    if role == AdminRole.SUPER_ADMIN:
        return ALL_PERMISSIONS
    return ROLE_PERMISSIONS.get(role, frozenset())


def role_can(role: str, permission: str) -> bool:
    """Whether ``role`` may exercise ``permission`` — the one authority check."""
    return permission in permissions_for(role)


def mfa_required(role: str) -> bool:
    return role in MFA_REQUIRED_ROLES
```

"""Public (unauthenticated) endpoints backed by console models.

The marketing "Get started" lead intake and the "Contact us" message intake
live here. They are deliberately open (``AllowAny``, no auth) because they are
called from the public marketing site before anyone has an account. A honeypot
field defends against bots.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from drf_spectacular.utils import extend_schema
from rest_framework.permissions import AllowAny
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.throttling import AnonRateThrottle
from rest_framework.views import APIView

from console.serializers_contact import ContactMessageCreateSerializer
from console.serializers_leads import LeadCreateSerializer


class LeadIntakeThrottle(AnonRateThrottle):
    scope = "lead_intake"


class PublicLeadCreateView(APIView):
    """POST /leads — capture a "Get started" lead from the marketing site."""

    authentication_classes: list = []
    permission_classes = [AllowAny]
    throttle_classes = [LeadIntakeThrottle]

    @extend_schema(request=LeadCreateSerializer, responses={201: None})
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        serializer = LeadCreateSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)

        # Honeypot: a bot fills this hidden field — accept silently, save nothing.
        if serializer.validated_data.get("botcheck"):
            return Response(status=201)

        serializer.save()
        return Response(status=201)


class PublicContactCreateView(APIView):
    """POST /contact — capture a support/contact message from the marketing site."""

    authentication_classes: list = []
    permission_classes = [AllowAny]
    throttle_classes = [LeadIntakeThrottle]

    @extend_schema(request=ContactMessageCreateSerializer, responses={201: None})
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        serializer = ContactMessageCreateSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)

        # Honeypot: a bot fills this hidden field — accept silently, save nothing.
        if serializer.validated_data.get("botcheck"):
            return Response(status=201)

        serializer.save()
        return Response(status=201)
=== PERMISSIONS ===
"""Admin permission classes + the base view every admin endpoint extends.

``AdminAPIView`` centralises the three guarantees every admin endpoint needs:
admin-only auth, a role gate, and the deliberate cross-tenant access (it never
applies ``for_merchant`` scoping — that inversion lives here, not scattered).

Since Phase 12 every gate derives from the central matrix in ``console.rbac``:
the named per-domain classes below are thin ``require(...)`` aliases, and new
endpoints gate with ``require(Permission.X)`` directly. There is one source of
truth for who-can-do-what — the matrix — not scattered role checks.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import ClassVar

from rest_framework.permissions import BasePermission
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.views import APIView

from console.auth import AdminJWTAuthentication
from console.models import AdminUser
from console.rbac import Permission, role_can


class IsAdminUser(BasePermission):
    """Any authenticated, active platform admin."""

    def has_permission(self, request: Request, view: APIView) -> bool:
        return isinstance(request.user, AdminUser) and request.user.is_active


class IsSuperAdmin(BasePermission):
    def has_permission(self, request: Request, view: APIView) -> bool:
        return isinstance(request.user, AdminUser) and request.user.is_super_admin


class _MatrixPermission(BasePermission):
    """Grant when the active admin's role holds ``required_permission`` in the
    RBAC matrix. Super-admin holds every permission (see ``rbac.permissions_for``)."""

    required_permission: ClassVar[str] = ""

    def has_permission(self, request: Request, view: APIView) -> bool:
        admin = request.user
        return (
            isinstance(admin, AdminUser)
            and admin.is_active
            and role_can(admin.role, self.required_permission)
        )


def require(permission: str) -> type[_MatrixPermission]:
    """Build a matrix-backed permission class for ``permission`` (use inline in
    ``get_permissions`` or ``permission_classes``)."""

    return type(
        f"Require_{permission.replace('.', '_')}",
        (_MatrixPermission,),
        {"required_permission": permission},
```

"""Inbound "Get started" lead tests.

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from console.auth import issue_admin_tokens
from console.enums import AdminRole
from console.models import AdminAuditLog, AdminUser, Lead

pytestmark = pytest.mark.django_db

PUBLIC = "/api/v1/leads"
ADMIN = "/api/admin/v1/leads"

    "name": "Ali Hassan",
    "email": "ali@bloomcafe.com",
    "phone": "01000000000",

# ── Public intake ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_public_can_create_lead_without_auth():

def test_missing_fields_rejected():

    assert res.status_code == 400
    assert Lead.objects.count() == 0


def test_honeypot_is_accepted_but_saves_nothing():
    res = APIClient().post(PUBLIC, {**VALID, "botcheck": "spam"}, format="json")
    assert res.status_code == 201
    assert Lead.objects.count() == 0


# ── Admin management ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def test_admin_lists_leads(super_admin):
    Lead.objects.create(**VALID)
    res = _admin(super_admin).get(ADMIN)
    assert res.status_code == 200
    assert len(res.data) == 1
    assert res.data[0]["email"] == "ali@bloomcafe.com"


def test_admin_requires_auth():
    Lead.objects.create(**VALID)
    assert APIClient().get(ADMIN).status_code in (401, 403)


def test_mark_contacted_sets_timestamp_and_audits(super_admin):
    lead = Lead.objects.create(**VALID)
    res = _admin(super_admin).patch(f"{ADMIN}/{lead.id}", {"status": "contacted"}, format="json")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    lead.refresh_from_db()
    assert lead.status == Lead.Status.CONTACTED
    assert lead.contacted_at is not None
    assert AdminAuditLog.objects.filter(action="lead.update").exists()


def test_delete_lead(super_admin):
    lead = Lead.objects.create(**VALID)
    res = _admin(super_admin).delete(f"{ADMIN}/{lead.id}")
    assert res.status_code == 204
    assert Lead.objects.count() == 0
    assert AdminAuditLog.objects.filter(action="lead.delete").exists()

can never authenticate an admin endpoint (see ``console.auth``). Passwords use

Seeding and\n# the \"is this slug a system value?\" check both read this map, so adding a new\n# configurable dropdown means adding it here and nowhere else.\nSYSTEM_CHOICES: dict[str, type[models.TextChoices]] = {\n    CrmChoiceKind.STATUS: LeadStatus,\n    CrmChoiceKind.PRIORITY: LeadPriority,\n    CrmChoiceKind.TEMPERATURE: LeadTemperature,\n    CrmChoiceKind.SOURCE: LeadSource,\n    CrmChoiceKind.EXPECTED_PLAN: ExpectedPlan,\n    CrmChoiceKind.CONTACT_METHOD: ContactMethod,\n    CrmChoiceKind.NEXT_ACTION: NextAction,\n}\n\n\ndef is_system_value(kind: str, slug: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether ``slug`` is a code-level value of ``kind`` (so undeletable).\"\"\"\n    enum = SYSTEM_CHOICES.get(kind)\n    return bool(enum) and slug in enum.values\n\n\n# ── Lead scoring ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n# Weights sum to exactly 100 at maximum (high + hot + website + demo + proposal\n# + 5 calls + recent activity), so the score needs no clamping to stay in range\n# and a full bar genuinely means \"every signal fired\".\n#\n# They are also tuned so a fresh website lead — medium priority, warm, one form\n# submission, no calls, activity today — lands on exactly 25 (8 + 12 + 5), the\n# starting score the spec calls for. Unsaved lead: no related rows to count yet, and .filter() would raise.\n    if lead.pk is None:\n        return min(score, SCORE_MAX)\n\n    milestones = set(\n        lead.activities.filter(\n            kind__in=[ActivityKind.DEMO_SCHEDULED, ActivityKind.PROPOSAL_SENT]\n        ).values_list(\"kind\", flat=True)\n    )\n    if ActivityKind.DEMO_SCHEDULED in milestones:\n        score += _DEMO_SCHEDULED_POINTS\n    if ActivityKind.PROPOSAL_SENT in milestones:\n        score += _PROPOSAL_SENT_POINTS\n\n    calls = lead.calls.count()\n    score += min(calls, _MAX_SCORED_CALLS) * _POINTS_PER_CALL\n\n    cutoff = timezone.now() - _RECENT_ACTIVITY_WINDOW\n    if lead.activities.filter(created_at__gte=cutoff).exists():\n        score += _RECENT_ACTIVITY_POINTS\n\n    return min(score, SCORE_MAX)\n",

{
  "content" : "\"\"\"Seeding for the configurable CRM dropdowns.\n\n``ensure_seeded`` materialises one ``CrmChoice`` row per code-level value in\n``crm.SYSTEM_CHOICES``, so Settings → CRM Configuration has something to show on\na fresh install and every system value arrives pre-labelled and pre-coloured.\n\nIt is idempotent and *non-destructive*: an existing row is never overwritten,\nbecause an admin may have re-labelled or re-coloured it and their edit outranks\nour default. It only ever fills gaps — which is what makes it safe to re-run\nfrom a data migration on every release when a new enum value lands.\n\nThe one thing it does force is ``is_system=True``: that flag is the code's\nclaim, not the admin's, and it is what stops the row being deleted.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom console import crm\n\n# Badge colours for the values worth distinguishing at a glance. Anything absent\n# seeds with an empty colour and renders in the console's neutral badge — that is\n# a deliberate default, not an omission: colouring all 24 statuses would make the\n# table louder without making it more readable.\n_DEFAULT_COLORS: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {\n    crm.CrmChoiceKind.STATUS: {\n        crm.LeadStatus.NEW_LEAD: \"#3b82f6\",  # blue — untouched\n        crm.LeadStatus.INTERESTED: \"#8b5cf6\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.VERY_INTERESTED: \"#7c3aed\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.HOT_LEAD: \"#ef4444\",  # red — move now\n        crm.LeadStatus.DEMO_SCHEDULED: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.DEMO_COMPLETED: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.PROPOSAL_SENT: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.NEGOTIATION: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.CUSTOMER: \"#10b981\",  # green — won\n        crm.LeadStatus.CONVERTED: \"#059669\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.NOT_INTERESTED: \"#6b7280\",  # grey — dead\n        crm.LeadStatus.TOO_EXPENSIVE: \"#6b7280\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.USING_COMPETITOR: \"#6b7280\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.DO_NOT_CALL_AGAIN: \"#4b5563\",\n        crm.LeadStatus.CLOSED: \"#6b7280\",\n    },\n    crm.CrmChoiceKind.PRIORITY: {\n        crm.LeadPriority.HIGH: \"#ef4444\",\n        crm.LeadPriority.MEDIUM: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadPriority.LOW: \"#6b7280\",\n    },\n    crm.CrmChoiceKind.TEMPERATURE: {\n        crm.LeadTemperature.HOT: \"#ef4444\",\n        crm.LeadTemperature.WARM: \"#f59e0b\",\n        crm.LeadTemperature.COLD: \"#3b82f6\",\n    },\n}\n\n# Categories ship with the verticals Stampn actually sells to, so the dropdown\n# is useful on day one. Unlike every other kind these are NOT system rows —\n# there is no enum behind them and no code reads them, so an admin may rename or\n# delete any of these freely.\n_SEED_CATEGORIES: tuple[str, ...] = (\n    \"Café\",\n    \"Restaurant\",\n    \"Bakery\",\n    \"Juice Bar\",\n    \"Salon\",\n    \"Barber Shop\",\n    \"Spa\",\n    \"Gym\",\n    \"Pharmacy\",\n    \"Retail Shop\",\n    \"Other\",\n)\n\n\ndef ensure_seeded(choice_model=None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create any missing system rows (and the starter categories). Returns the\n    number of rows created.\n\n    ``choice_model`` lets a migration pass its historical ``CrmChoice`` — inside\n    a migration the real model may not match the frozen schema, so never import\n    it directly there.\n    \"\"\"\n    if choice_model is None:  # pragma: no cover — exercised via the management command\n        from console.models import CrmChoice as choice_model  # noqa: N813\n\n    created = 0\n    for kind, enum in crm.SYSTEM_CHOICES.items():\n        colors = _DEFAULT_COLORS.get(kind, {})\n        for order, value in enumerate(enum.values):\n            _, was_created = choice_model.objects.get_or_create(\n                kind=kind,\n                slug=value,\n                defaults={\n                    \"label\": enum(value).label,\n                    \"color\": colors.get(value, \"\"),\n                    \"order\": order,\n                    \"is_system\": True,\n                    \"is_active\": True,\n                },\n            )\n            created += int(was_created)\n\n        # A pre-existing row must still be flagged system — the flag is the\n        # code's claim on the slug, and it is what refuses the delete.\n        choice_model.objects.filter(kind=kind, slug__in=list(enum.values)).exclude(\n            is_system=True\n        ).update(is_system=True)\n\n    for order, label in enumerate(_SEED_CATEGORIES):\n        _, was_created = choice_model.objects.get_or_create(\n            kind=crm.CrmChoiceKind.CATEGORY,\n            slug=label.lower().replace(\" \", \"_\").replace(\"é\", \"e\"),\n            defaults={\"label\": label, \"order\": order, \"is_system\": False, \"is_active\": True},\n        )\n        created += int(was_created)\n\n    return created\n",

}

{
  "content" : "\"\"\"Move the leads that already exist onto the CRM vocabulary.\n\n0013 widened the schema; this fills it in. Every pre-CRM lead came from the\nmarketing form — that was the only thing that could create one — so they all\nbackfill as website leads created by the system.\n\nThe status remap matters most: the old field held ``new`` \/ ``contacted``, and\n0013 left those strings sitting in rows that the new choices no longer name.\nDjango does not enforce choices at the database level, so nothing has broken\nloudly — the values are simply unreadable to the new code, which is exactly the\nkind of quiet wrongness worth fixing in the same release that causes it.\n\n``contacted`` maps to ``contact_attempted`` rather than one of the richer\n\"answered\" statuses: the old model recorded only that someone reached out, not\nhow it went, and inventing a warmer status than the data supports would put\nleads in front of sales as more qualified than they are.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom django.db import migrations\n\nfrom console.crm_seed import ensure_seeded\n\n# old value → new value. Anything else (there should be nothing) is left alone\n# and lands on the model default at next save.\n_STATUS_REMAP = {\n    \"new\": \"new_lead\",\n    \"contacted\": \"contact_attempted\",\n}\n\n# A website lead's starting score. Not a magic number: it is what\n# ``crm.score_lead`` computes for medium priority + warm + a website submission\n# with no calls yet (8 + 12 + 5). Hard-coded here because a migration must not\n# import live scoring logic that may be re-tuned in a later release.\n_WEBSITE_START_SCORE = 25\n\n\ndef backfill(apps, schema_editor):\n    Lead = apps.get_model(\"console\", \"Lead\")\n    LeadActivity = apps.get_model(\"console\", \"LeadActivity\")\n    CrmChoice = apps.get_model(\"console\", \"CrmChoice\")\n\n    ensure_seeded(CrmChoice)\n\n    for old, new in _STATUS_REMAP.items():\n        Lead.objects.filter(status=old).update(status=new)\n\n    Lead.objects.update(\n        lead_type=\"website\",\n        source=\"website\",\n        created_by_type=\"system\",\n        priority=\"medium\",\n        temperature=\"warm\",\n        lead_score=_WEBSITE_START_SCORE,\n        last_activity=\"Website Form Submitted\",\n    )\n\n    # Give each existing lead the timeline entry it would have had if the CRM\n    # had existed when it arrived, so the details page is never blank. Dated to\n    # the lead's own created_at, not now — the submission happened when it\n    # happened. (auto_now_add ignores an assigned value on insert, hence the\n    # second pass to set it.)\n    existing = set(LeadActivity.objects.values_list(\"lead_id\", flat=True))\n    for lead in Lead.objects.exclude(id__in=existing).iterator():\n        activity = LeadActivity.objects.create(\n            lead_id=lead.id,\n            kind=\"website_form_submitted\",\n            title=\"Website Form Submitted\",\n            description=f\"{lead.name} submitted the Get started form.\",\n            actor_label=\"System\",\n        )\n        LeadActivity.objects.filter(pk=activity.pk).update(created_at=lead.created_at)\n\n\ndef unbackfill(apps, schema_editor):\n    \"\"\"Put the two old status values back so 0013 can reverse cleanly.\"\"\"\n    Lead = apps.get_model(\"console\", \"Lead\")\n    for old, new in _STATUS_REMAP.items():\n        Lead.objects.filter(status=new).update(status=old)\n\n\nclass Migration(migrations.Migration):\n    dependencies = [(\"console\", \"0013_crm_lead_expansion\")]\n\n    operations = [migrations.RunPython(backfill, unbackfill)]\n",

  "content" : "\"\"\"Lead orchestration — the rules that must hold no matter who calls.\n\nViews handle HTTP; this module handles what a lead *means*. It exists because\nthree invariants have to survive every entry point (public form, console, later\nthe CSV import), and a rule re-implemented per caller is a rule that drifts:\n\n* every meaningful change lands on the timeline, automatically;\n* ``last_activity`` and ``lead_score`` follow the timeline rather than being\n  set by hand; and\n* a website lead is born with exactly the fields the spec fixes for it.\n\nThe timeline is the reason ``log_activity`` is the only way to write an\nactivity: it also updates the lead's denormalised ``last_activity`` and\nre-scores, and those three writes are one logical act.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom django.db import transaction\nfrom django.db.models import Q\nfrom django.utils import timezone\n\nfrom console import crm\nfrom console.models import AdminUser, Lead, LeadActivity\n\n\ndef _actor_label(actor: AdminUser | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How the timeline names whoever did this. Snapshotted at write time.\"\"\"\n    if actor is None:\n        return \"System\"\n    return actor.name or actor.email\n\n\ndef log_activity(\n    lead: Lead,\n    kind: str,\n    title: str,\n    *,\n    description: str = \"\",\n    actor: AdminUser | None = None,\n    rescore: bool = True,\n) -> LeadActivity:\n    \"\"\"Append one entry to ``lead``'s timeline and refresh its derived state.\n\n    The single writer for activities. ``rescore`` exists only for callers that\n    write several activities in one act (conversion) and would otherwise score\n    the same lead repeatedly — the last call leaves it correct either way, since\n    scoring is computed from scratch rather than incremented.\n    \"\"\"\n    activity = LeadActivity.objects.create(\n        lead=lead,\n        kind=kind,\n        title=title,\n        description=description,\n        actor=actor,\n        actor_label=_actor_label(actor),\n    )\n    lead.last_activity = title\n    lead.save(update_fields=[\"last_activity\", \"updated_at\"])\n    if rescore:\n        lead.recalculate_score()\n    return activity\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef create_website_lead(**fields: Any) -> Lead:\n    \"\"\"Create a lead from the public marketing form.\n\n    Every CRM field is fixed here rather than defaulted on the model: the model\n    defaults describe a *manual* lead (the common case in the console), and a\n    website lead's shape is a spec'd contract — type, source, unassigned, warm,\n    medium, starting score — that should read in one place.\n    \"\"\"\n    lead = Lead.objects.create(\n        **fields,\n        lead_type=crm.LeadType.WEBSITE,\n        source=crm.LeadSource.WEBSITE,\n        created_by_type=crm.LeadCreatedBy.SYSTEM,\n        created_by=None,\n        assigned_sales=None,\n        status=crm.LeadStatus.NEW_LEAD,\n        priority=crm.LeadPriority.MEDIUM,\n        temperature=crm.LeadTemperature.WARM,\n    )\n    log_activity(\n        lead,\n        crm.ActivityKind.WEBSITE_FORM_SUBMITTED,\n        \"Website Form Submitted\",\n        description=f\"{lead.name} submitted the Get started form.\",\n        actor=None,\n    )\n    return lead\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef create_manual_lead(*, actor: AdminUser, **fields: Any) -> Lead:\n    \"\"\"Create a lead by hand from the console. ``source`` is the caller's to\n    choose (a walk-in and a referral are both manual); type and creator are not.\"\"\"\n    fields.setdefault(\"source\", crm.LeadSource.MANUAL)\n    lead = Lead.objects.create(\n        **fields,\n        lead_type=crm.LeadType.MANUAL,\n        created_by_type=crm.LeadCreatedBy.SALES_USER,\n        created_by=actor,\n    )\n    log_activity(\n        lead,\n        crm.ActivityKind.MANUAL_LEAD_CREATED,\n        \"Manual Lead Created\",\n        description=f\"Added by {_actor_label(actor)}.\",\n        actor=actor,\n    )\n    return lead\n\n\n# Which field change writes which timeline entry. Only the changes a sales user\n# would want to see in the story of the lead — editing a typo'd address is not\n# one of them, and a timeline that logs everything gets read for nothing.\n_TRACKED_FIELDS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {\n    \"status\": (crm.ActivityKind.STATUS_CHANGED, \"Status Changed\"),\n    \"priority\": (crm.ActivityKind.PRIORITY_CHANGED, \"Priority Changed\"),\n    \"assigned_sales\": (crm.ActivityKind.ASSIGNED_SALES_CHANGED, \"Assigned Sales Changed\"),\n}\n\n# Statuses that are milestones in their own right: reaching one writes its own\n# entry as well as the status-change entry, because scoring reads these from the\n# timeline and a lead that passes through \"Proposal Sent\" must keep the credit\n# even after it moves on to \"Negotiation\".\n_MILESTONE_STATUSES: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {\n    crm.LeadStatus.DEMO_SCHEDULED: (crm.ActivityKind.DEMO_SCHEDULED, \"Demo Scheduled\"),\n    crm.LeadStatus.DEMO_COMPLETED: (crm.ActivityKind.DEMO_COMPLETED, \"Demo Completed\"),\n    crm.LeadStatus.PROPOSAL_SENT: (crm.ActivityKind.PROPOSAL_SENT, \"Proposal Sent\"),\n    crm.LeadStatus.CLOSED: (crm.ActivityKind.CLOSED, \"Closed\"),\n}\n\n\ndef _display(lead: Lead, field: str) -> str:\n    value = getattr(lead, field)\n    if isinstance(value, AdminUser):\n        return _actor_label(value)\n    if value in (None, \"\"):\n        return \"—\"\n    return str(dict(_choices_for(field)).get(value, value))\n\n\ndef _choices_for(field: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return list(Lead._meta.get_field(field).choices or [])\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef apply_update(lead: Lead, changes: dict[str, Any], *, actor: AdminUser | None) -> Lead:\n    \"\"\"Apply ``changes`` to ``lead``, logging the ones that tell its story.\n\n    Reads the old values *before* writing so the timeline can say what changed\n    from what — the thing a sales user actually wants when they open a lead they\n    have not touched in three weeks.\n    \"\"\"\n    before = {field: getattr(lead, field) for field in _TRACKED_FIELDS}\n\n    for field, value in changes.items():\n        setattr(lead, field, value)\n\n    # Contacting a lead is what \"contacted_at\" has always meant; keep the old\n    # column truthful now that a dedicated \"contacted\" status no longer exists.\n    if \"status\" in changes and lead.status != crm.LeadStatus.NEW_LEAD and lead.contacted_at is None:\n        lead.contacted_at = timezone.now()\n        changes[\"contacted_at\"] = lead.contacted_at\n\n    lead.save()\n\n    for field, (kind, title) in _TRACKED_FIELDS.items():\n        if field not in changes or before[field] == getattr(lead, field):\n            continue\n        old_lead = Lead(**{field: before[field]})\n        log_activity(\n            lead,\n            kind,\n            title,\n            description=f\"{_display(old_lead, field)} → {_display(lead, field)}\",\n            actor=actor,\n            rescore=False,\n        )\n\n    new_status = changes.get(\"status\")\n    if new_status in _MILESTONE_STATUSES and before[\"status\"] != new_status:\n        kind, title = _MILESTONE_STATUSES[new_status]\n        log_activity(lead, kind, title, actor=actor, rescore=False)\n\n    lead.recalculate_score()\n    return lead\n\n\ndef find_duplicates(\n    *, phone: str = \"\", email: str = \"\", business_name: str = \"\", exclude_id=None\n):\n    \"\"\"Leads that may already be this one.\n\n    Phone and email match exactly; business name matches case-insensitively and\n    whole, not as a substring — \"Bloom\" must not collide with every café in\n    Cairo whose name contains it. Deliberately advisory: the caller decides\n    whether a hit blocks, merges, or is ignored, because a shop with two\n    branches legitimately has two leads on one phone number.\n    \"\"\"\n    probes = Q()\n    if phone:\n        probes |= Q(phone=phone)\n    if email:\n        probes |= Q(email__iexact=email)\n    if business_name:\n        probes |= Q(business_name__iexact=business_name.strip())\n    if not probes:\n        return Lead.objects.none()\n\n    matches = Lead.objects.filter(probes)\n    if exclude_id:\n        matches = matches.exclude(pk=exclude_id)\n    return matches.select_related(\"assigned_sales\")\n",

"""Admin console views for inbound support/contact messages.

Any active admin may view the list and mark a message read/unread or delete it.
The public intake that creates these lives in ``console.public``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.mail import EmailMultiAlternatives
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.utils import timezone
from drf_spectacular.utils import extend_schema
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.response import Response

from console import audit
from console.models import ContactMessage
from console.permissions import AdminAPIView
from console.serializers_contact import (
    AdminContactMessageCreateSerializer,
    ContactMessageSerializer,
    ContactReplySerializer,
)


class ContactMessageListView(AdminAPIView):
    """GET /messages — list · POST /messages — admin-created message."""

    @extend_schema(responses=ContactMessageSerializer(many=True))
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        return Response(ContactMessageSerializer(ContactMessage.objects.all(), many=True).data)

    @extend_schema(request=AdminContactMessageCreateSerializer, responses=ContactMessageSerializer)
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        """Create a contact message manually so the admin can then reply to it."""
        serializer = AdminContactMessageCreateSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        message = serializer.save()
        audit.record(
            request,
            "contact_message.create",
            target_type="contact_message",
            target_id=str(message.id),
            metadata={"email": message.email, "subject": message.subject},
        )
        return Response(ContactMessageSerializer(message).data, status=201)


class ContactMessageDetailView(AdminAPIView):
    """PATCH /messages/{id} — toggle read status · DELETE /messages/{id}."""

    @extend_schema(request=None, responses=ContactMessageSerializer)
    def patch(self, request: Request, message_id: str) -> Response:
        message = get_object_or_404(ContactMessage, pk=message_id)
        status = (request.data.get("status") or ContactMessage.Status.READ).strip()
        if status not in ContactMessage.Status.values:
            return Response(
                {"error": {"code": "INVALID_STATUS", "message": "Unknown message status."}},

"""Cursor pagination (contract §3.7).

List endpoints return ``{ "next", "previous", "results" }``. Cursor pagination
keeps results stable as rows are added during paging.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from rest_framework.pagination import CursorPagination

from core import constants


class DefaultCursorPagination(CursorPagination):
    page_size = constants.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
    page_size_query_param = "page_size"
    max_page_size = constants.MAX_PAGE_SIZE
    ordering = "-created_at"

    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        qs = m.apply_filters(m.merchant_queryset(), request.query_params)

        paginator = DefaultCursorPagination()
        page = paginator.paginate_queryset(qs, request, view=self) or []
        rows = [self._row(mer) for mer in page]
        return paginator.get_paginated_response(MerchantListSerializer(rows, many=True).data)

        return {

A whitelist, not ``order_by(param)``: that would\n# hand any caller the ability to sort by — and therefore probe — any column on\n# the model, and would 500 on a typo.\nSORTABLE: frozenset[str] = frozenset(\n    {\n        \"business_name\",\n        \"name\",\n        \"area\",\n        \"priority\",\n        \"status\",\n        \"temperature\",\n        \"lead_score\",\n        \"lead_type\",\n        \"source\",\n        \"next_follow_up_at\",\n        \"last_contact_at\",\n        \"created_at\",\n    }\n)\n\n# Exact-match filters: query param → model field. Each accepts a repeated param\n# (?status=a&status=b) and ORs the values, which is what the multi-select filter\n# chips in the console send.\n_EXACT_FILTERS: dict[str, str] = {\n    \"lead_type\": \"lead_type\",\n    \"status\": \"status\",\n    \"priority\": \"priority\",\n    \"temperature\": \"temperature\",\n    \"source\": \"source\",\n    \"category\": \"category\",\n    \"assigned_sales\": \"assigned_sales_id\",\n}\n\n\ndef lead_queryset() -> QuerySet[Lead]:\n    \"\"\"The base queryset every lead read starts from. ``select_related`` is not\n    an optimisation detail here — the table serialises both admins on every row,\n    so without it a 50-row page costs 100 extra queries.\"\"\"\n    return Lead.objects.select_related(\"assigned_sales\", \"created_by\", \"converted_merchant\")\n\n\ndef _parse_date(value: str) -> datetime | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse a ``YYYY-MM-DD`` filter bound into an aware datetime, or None if it\n    is not a date. Bad input filters nothing rather than 500ing — a filter bar\n    is not a place to punish a typo.\"\"\"\n    parsed = timezone.datetime.strptime(value, \"%Y-%m-%d\") if len(value) == 10 else None\n    if parsed is None:\n        return None\n    return timezone.make_aware(parsed, timezone.get_current_timezone())\n\n\ndef apply_filters(qs: QuerySet[Lead], params) -> QuerySet[Lead]:\n    \"\"\"Narrow ``qs`` by the table's filter bar.\n\n    Unknown params are ignored, and an empty value is treated as \"no filter\" —\n    the console sends ``?status=`` when a user clears a chip, and that must mean\n    all statuses, not no leads.\n    \"\"\"\n    for param, field in _EXACT_FILTERS.items():\n        values = [v for v in params.getlist(param) if v]\n        if values:\n            qs = qs.filter(**{f\"{field}__in\": values})\n\n    # Unassigned is a first-class filter — it is the \"who is not working these?\"\n    # question — and cannot be expressed by ?assigned_sales=<id>.\n    if params.get(\"unassigned\") in (\"1\", \"true\"):\n        qs = qs.filter(assigned_sales__isnull=True)\n\n    if area := params.get(\"area\", \"\").strip():\n        qs = qs.filter(area__icontains=area)\n\n    for param, field in (\n        (\"created_from\", \"created_at__gte\"),\n        (\"created_to\", \"created_at__lt\"),\n        (\"follow_up_from\", \"next_follow_up_at__gte\"),\n        (\"follow_up_to\", \"next_follow_up_at__lt\"),\n    ):\n        raw = params.get(param, \"\").strip()\n        if not raw:\n            continue\n        bound = _parse_date(raw)\n        if bound is None:\n            continue\n        # \"_to\" is inclusive of the whole day the user picked — they mean \"up to\n        # and including the 5th\", not \"up to midnight as the 5th begins\".\n        if param.endswith(\"_to\"):\n            bound += timezone.timedelta(days=1)\n        qs = qs.filter(**{field: bound})\n\n    if q := params.get(\"q\", \"\").strip():\n        qs = qs.filter(\n            Q(business_name__icontains=q)\n            | Q(name__icontains=q)\n            | Q(phone__icontains=q)\n            | Q(whatsapp__icontains=q)\n            | Q(email__icontains=q)\n            | Q(area__icontains=q)\n        )\n\n    return qs\n\n\ndef apply_sort(qs: QuerySet[Lead], params) -> tuple[QuerySet[Lead], tuple[str, ...]]:\n    \"\"\"Order ``qs`` by ``?sort=`` (prefix ``-`` for descending), defaulting to\n    newest first. Returns the ordering too, because cursor pagination needs to\n    be told the same thing the queryset was.\n\n    Always tie-breaks on ``-created_at``: cursor pagination walks the ordering\n    to find its place, so a sort on a non-unique column (every lead is \"medium\"\n    priority) without a unique tiebreak can skip or repeat rows across pages.\n    \"\"\"\n    raw = params.get(\"sort\", \"\").strip()\n    field = raw.lstrip(\"-\")\n    if not field or field not in SORTABLE:\n        return qs.order_by(\"-created_at\"), (\"-created_at\",)\n\n    if field == \"created_at\":\n        ordering = (raw,)\n    else:\n        ordering = (raw, \"-created_at\")\n    return qs.order_by(*ordering), ordering\n\n\ndef kpis(qs: QuerySet[Lead] | None = None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The dashboard cards, in one query plus two.\n\n    Computed over the *filtered* queryset the caller passes, so the cards\n    describe what the table below them is showing rather than contradicting it.\n timezone.make_aware(\n        datetime.combine(timezone.localtime(now).date(), time.min), tz\n    )\n    today_end = today_start + timezone.timedelta(days=1)\n\n    counts = qs.aggregate(\n        total=Count(\"id\"),\n        website=Count(\"id\", filter=Q(lead_type=crm.LeadType.WEBSITE)),\n        manual=Count(\"id\", filter=Q(lead_type=crm.LeadType.MANUAL)),\n        interested=Count(\"id\", filter=Q(status=crm.LeadStatus.INTERESTED)),\n        demo_scheduled=Count(\"id\", filter=Q(status=crm.LeadStatus.DEMO_SCHEDULED)),\n        customers=Count(\n            \"id\", filter=Q(status__in=[crm.LeadStatus.CUSTOMER, crm.LeadStatus.CONVERTED])\n        ),\n        converted=Count(\"id\", filter=Q(converted_merchant__isnull=False)),\n        follow_ups_today=Count(\n            \"id\", filter=Q(next_follow_up_at__gte=today_start, next_follow_up_at__lt=today_end)\n        ),\n        # Overdue skips leads that are already done — chasing a follow-up on a\n        # lead that said \"do not call again\" is not a task, it is a mistake.\n        overdue_follow_ups=Count(\n            \"id\",\n            filter=Q(next_follow_up_at__lt=now) & ~Q(status__in=crm.TERMINAL_STATUSES),\n        ),\n    )\n\n    total = counts[\"total\"]\n    converted = counts.pop(\"converted\")\n    counts[\"calls_today\"] = LeadCall.objects.filter(\n        lead__in=qs, called_at__gte=today_start, called_at__lt=today_end\n    ).count()\n    counts[\"conversion_rate\"] = round(converted \/ total * 100, 1) if total else 0.0\n    return counts\n",

@extend_schema(responses=LeadSerializer(many=True))\n    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:\n        qs = lead_query.apply_filters(lead_query.lead_queryset(), request.query_params)\n        qs, ordering = lead_query.apply_sort(qs, request.query_params)\n\n        paginator = _LeadCursorPagination(ordering)\n        page = paginator.paginate_queryset(qs, request, view=self) or []\n        return paginator.get_paginated_response(LeadSerializer(page, many=True).data)\n\n    @extend_schema(request=LeadWriteSerializer, responses=LeadDetailSerializer)\n    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:\n        serializer = LeadWriteSerializer(data=request.data)\n        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)\n        data = serializer.validated_data\n\n        # Duplicate detection is advisory, and opt-out by design: a shop with two\n        # branches legitimately has two leads on one phone number, so the caller\n        # decides. business_name=data.get(\"business_name\", \"\"),\n            )\n            if duplicates.exists():\n                return Response(\n                    {\n                        \"error\": {\n                            \"code\": \"POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE\",\n                            \"message\": (\n                                \"A lead with this phone, email or business name already exists.\"\n                            ),\n                            \"duplicates\": LeadSerializer(duplicates[:5], many=True).data,\n                        }\n                    },\n                    status=409,\n                )\n\n        lead = crm_service.create_manual_lead(actor=request.user, **data)\n        audit.record(\n            request,\n            \"lead.create\",\n The unique-together constraint is firing during serializer validation, so my `RESERVED_SLUG` guard never runs — the caller gets a generic 400 instead of the explanation. The fix is to let the view own that check:

## 201 · Claude

_(no text response)_

### 202 · Tool: Edit

```json
{
  "file_path" : "\/Users\/momen\/My Projects\/Kasbana\/backend\/console\/serializers_leads.py",
  "new_string" : "class CrmChoiceSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):\n    \"\"\"A configurable dropdown row. ``is_system`` is the code's claim on a slug,\n    never the client's to set.\n\n    ``validators = []`` drops DRF's implicit unique-together check on\n    (kind, slug). Not to weaken it — the database constraint still holds, and\n    ``views_crm_config`` re-checks — but because that validator answers a\n    collision with a bare \"must be unique\" 400, which cannot distinguish \"you\n    already added this\" from \"this is a built-in you may not shadow\". Those need\n    different fixes, so the view owns the check and says which one it is.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    class Meta:\n        model = CrmChoice\n        fields = [\"id\", \"kind\", \"slug\", \"label\", \"color\", \"order\", \"is_system\", \"is_active\"]\n        read_only_fields = [\"id\", \"is_system\"]\n        validators: list = []",
  "old_string" : "class CrmChoiceSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):\n    \"\"\"A configurable dropdown row. ``is_system`` is the code's claim on a slug,\n    never the client's to set.\"\"\"\n\n    class Meta:\n        model = CrmChoice\n        fields = [\"id\", \"kind\", \"slug\", \"label\", \"color\", \"order\", \"is_system\", \"is_active\"]\n        read_only_fields = [\"id\", \"is_system\"]",

}

# Runs the backend quality gate (ruff · black · mypy · pytest) on every push to
# dev and on pull requests that touch the backend or the API contract.
# Independent of distribute.yml — this gates code; that publishes branches.

on:
  push:
    branches: [dev]

      - "backend/**"
      - "contracts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/backend-ci.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "backend/**"
      - "contracts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/backend-ci.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: backend-ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: backend/requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Ruff (lint)

      - name: Black (format check)

      - name: Mypy (type check)

        env:
          DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: config.settings.dev

noqa: E402\nfrom django.db import connection  # noqa: E402\n\ncall_command(\"migrate\", \"console\", \"0012\", verbosity=0)\n\nwith connection.cursor() as c:\n    c.execute(\"DELETE FROM console_lead\")\n    for i, status in enumerate([\"new\", \"contacted\"]):\n        c.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO console_lead (id, created_at, updated_at, name, email, phone,\"\n            \" business_name, status, contacted_at) VALUES\"\n            \" (%s, '2026-01-05 10:00:00', '2026-01-05 10:00:00', %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, NULL)\",\n            [\n                f\"aaaaaaaa00000000000000000000000{i}\",\n                f\"Owner {i}\",\n                f\"o{i}@x.com\",\n                f\"0100000000{i}\",\n                f\"Shop {i}\",\n                status,\n            ],\n        )\n\ncall_command(\"migrate\", \"console\", verbosity=0)\n\nfrom console.models import CrmChoice, Lead, LeadActivity  # ## 310 · Claude

Stage 1 is done and every gate is green. I stopped here rather than continuing into the table and details page, per the staging you picked.

**What's built —** the CRM data layer, end to end:

- **`console/crm.py`** — the vocabulary (24 statuses, priorities, temperatures, sources, contact methods, next actions, expected plans, call results, activity kinds) plus scoring.
- **`console/models.py`** — `Lead` extended to the full CRM shape, plus `LeadActivity` (timeline), `LeadCall`, and `CrmChoice` (the configurable dropdowns).
- **`console/crm_service.py`** — the orchestration that keeps the timeline and score correct no matter who writes: website create, manual create, tracked updates, duplicate detection.
- **API** — filter/search/sort/paginate on `/leads`, `/leads/kpis`, `/leads/duplicates`, `/leads/{id}/calls`, and `/crm/choices`.
- **Migrations** — `0013` widens the schema, `0014` backfills existing leads and seeds 68 dropdown rows.
- **`SALES` role** with `LEADS_MANAGE` + `LEADS_CONVERT`, MFA-required like every other privileged role.

**Verification:** 881 backend tests pass (61 for leads, up from 7); ruff, black, mypy, Django check, migration check, and the OpenAPI contract are all clean; admin frontend lints, builds, and its 13 tests pass. I also ran the `0014` backfill against a database seeded with real pre-CRM rows — the case tests never exercise — and confirmed `new`/`contacted` remap correctly, existing leads get a timeline entry dated to their original submission, and the migration's hardcoded 25 matches what live scoring computes.

Three things worth knowing:

**I found and fixed a bug in my own scoring while the tests were blocked.** Every lead is born with a creation activity dated now, so the "recent activity" bonus was firing at birth — a fresh website lead scored 35, not the 25 you specified. Creation kinds are now excluded, so the signal means "is being worked" rather than "was created recently." That's the `test_creating_a_lead_is_not_engagement...` test.

**I made one judgment call you should sanity-check:** old `contacted` leads map to `contact_attempted`, not a warmer "answered" status. The old model only recorded *that* someone reached out, not how it went, and inventing a warmer status would put leads in front of sales as more qualified than the data supports.

**The existing Leads page still works but is deliberately minimal** — I patched it for the paginated response and new status slugs so `dev` isn't broken between stages. It's replaced wholesale by the real CRM table in Stage 2.

Remaining: the table + KPI cards, the details page, Convert-To-Merchant, and CSV import. Convert is the one I'd flag again — it should reuse the provisioning in `accounts/serializers.py` rather than grow a second path, which likely means extracting that first. Say the word and I'll start Stage 2.

import dayjs from 'dayjs'
import relativeTime from 'dayjs/plugin/relativeTime'

dayjs.extend(relativeTime)

export function fromNow(value) {
  return value ? dayjs(value).fromNow() : '—'
}

export function shortDate(value) {
  return value ? dayjs(value).format('DD MMM YYYY') : '—'
}

export function num(n) {
  return n == null ? '—' : Number(n).toLocaleString('en-US')
}

// Map a billing/merchant/invoice status string to a Badge tone.
export function statusTone(status) {
  const s = (status || '').toLowerCase()
  if (s === 'active' || s === 'paid') return 'success'
  if (s === 'trial' || s === 'trialing') return 'info'
  if (s === 'past_due' || s === 'suspended' || s === 'pending') return 'warn'
  if (s === 'locked' || s === 'canceled' || s === 'failed') return 'danger'
  return 'neutral'
}
// Admin API client — talks to /api/admin/v1 with the admin bearer token.
// On a 401 it tries a one-shot refresh, then forces re-login.
import axios from 'axios'
import { getAccess, getRefresh, setTokens, clearTokens } from './auth'

const BASE = (import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '') + '/api/admin/v1'

const api = axios.create({ baseURL: BASE })

api.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
  const token = getAccess()
  if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`
  return config
})

let refreshing = null

api.interceptors.response.use(
  (r) => r,
  async (error) => {
    const original = error.config
    const status = error.response?.status
    const refresh = getRefresh()
    if (status === 401 && refresh && !original._retried) {
      original._retried = true
      try {
        refreshing =
          refreshing ||
          axios.post(`${BASE}/auth/refresh`, { refresh }).finally(() => {
            refreshing = null
          })
        const { data } = await refreshing
        // Refresh ROTATES both tokens (Phase 15): we must persist the new refresh
        // too, or replaying the old one trips reuse-detection and kills the session.
        setTokens({ access: data.access, refresh: data.refresh })
        original.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${data.access}`

import { useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import api from '../../lib/api'

// Strip empty filter values so we don't send `?actor=` etc.
function clean(filters) {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(filters).filter(([, v]) => v !== '' && v != null))
}

// The audit trail, cursor-paginated. `next` is a full URL — we pull the cursor
// out of it for the following page so the list can grow with "Load more".
export function useAudit(filters) {
  const params = clean(filters)
  return useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: ['audit', params],
    queryFn: async ({ pageParam }) => {
      const q = pageParam ? { ...params, cursor: pageParam } : params
      return (await api.get('/audit', { params: q })).data
    },
    initialPageParam: null,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => {
      if (!lastPage.next) return undefined
      return new URL(lastPage.next).searchParams.get('cursor')
    },
  })
}

// CSV export of the filtered trail — authenticated blob download (a plain
// <a href> would miss the bearer token), mirroring the revenue export.
export async function downloadAuditCsv(filters) {
  const res = await api.get('/audit/export', { params: clean(filters), responseType: 'blob' })
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(res.data)
  const a = document.createElement('a')
  a.href = url
  a.download = 'audit_log.csv'
  document.body.appendChild(a)
  a.click()
  a.remove()
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url)
}

// Reusable step-up prompt: re-prove password (+ TOTP if the admin has MFA) to
// refresh the session's recent-auth window, then run `onConfirmed` (e.g. retry
// the sensitive action). Shown when an endpoint returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
export default function StepUpModal({ onClose, onConfirmed }) {
  const { admin } = useAuth()
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('')
  const [code, setCode] = useState('')
  const [err, setErr] = useState('')

  async function submit(e) {
    e.preventDefault()
    setErr('')
    setBusy(true)

      await onConfirmed()
      onClose()
    } catch (e2) {
      setErr(normalizeError(e2).message)

      setBusy(false)
    }
  }

          <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-tx">

            <h2 className="font-head font-semibold">Confirm it&apos;s you</h2>

59	def _parse_date(value: str) -> datetime | None:
60	    """Parse a ``YYYY-MM-DD`` filter bound into an aware datetime, or None if it
61	    is not one.
62	
63	    Unparseable input filters nothing rather than raising: a filter bar is not a
64	    place to punish a typo, and "17/07/2026" is a date-shaped string a person
65	    will genuinely type. Length-checking is not enough — that string is ten
66	    characters long and would still blow up strptime.
67	    """
68	    try:
69	        parsed = datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%d")
70	    except ValueError:
71	        return None
72	    return timezone.make_aware(parsed, timezone.get_current_timezone())

'w-full' : ''} rounded-ctl border border-line bg-surface px-3 py-2 text-sm text-tx placeholder:text-tx-3 focus:border-brand focus:outline-none`\n\nfunction Select({ value, onChange, label, full, children }) {\n  return (\n    <select value={value} onChange={onChange} className={selectClass(full)}>\n      <option value=\"\">{label}<\/option>\n      {children}\n    <\/select>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction Labelled({ label, children }) {\n  return (\n    <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n      {label}\n      {children}\n    <\/label>\n  )\n}\n",

{
  "content" : "import { ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ChevronsUpDown, Inbox, Globe, UserPlus } from 'lucide-react'\nimport Badge from '..\/..\/components\/Badge'\nimport { fromNow, shortDate } from '..\/..\/lib\/format'\nimport {\n  KIND,\n  PRIORITY_TONE,\n  TEMPERATURE_TONE,\n  colorFor,\n  labelFor,\n  scoreTone,\n  titleCase,\n} from '.\/crm'\n\n\/\/ Every column, in table order. `sort` is the API's sort key — a column without\n\/\/ one is not sortable, which is the honest signal for things the backend has no\n\/\/ index or ordering for.\n\/\/\n\/\/ `default: false` columns start hidden. The table shows fourteen columns' worth\n\/\/ of data; opening with all of them makes the first screen unreadable, so the\n\/\/ six that answer \"who do I call next\" are on and the rest are a click away.\nexport const COLUMNS = [\n  { key: 'business', label: 'Business', sort: 'business_name', always: true },\n  { key: 'owner', label: 'Owner', sort: 'name' },\n  { key: 'phone', label: 'Phone' },\n  { key: 'area', label: 'Area', sort: 'area', default: false },\n  { key: 'category', label: 'Category', default: false },\n  { key: 'assigned_sales', label: 'Assigned' },\n  { key: 'priority', label: 'Priority', sort: 'priority' },\n  { key: 'status', label: 'Status', sort: 'status' },\n  { key: 'temperature', label: 'Temp', sort: 'temperature', default: false },\n  { key: 'lead_score', label: 'Score', sort: 'lead_score' },\n  { key: 'lead_type', label: 'Type', sort: 'lead_type', default: false },\n  { key: 'source', label: 'Source', sort: 'source', default: false },\n  { key: 'next_follow_up_at', label: 'Next follow-up', sort: 'next_follow_up_at' },\n  { key: 'last_activity', label: 'Last activity', default: false },\n  { key: 'created_at', label: 'Created', sort: 'created_at' },\n]\n\nexport const DEFAULT_VISIBLE = COLUMNS.filter((c) => c.default !== false).map((c) => c.key)\n\nexport default function LeadsTable({\n  rows,\n  choices,\n  isLoading,\n  visible,\n  sort,\n  onSort,\n  selected,\n  onSelect,\n  onOpen,\n  hasFilters,\n}) {\n  const cols = COLUMNS.filter((c) => visible.includes(c.key))\n  const allSelected = rows.length > 0 && rows.every((r) => selected.has(r.id))\n\n  const toggleAll = () => onSelect(allSelected ? new Set() : new Set(rows.map((r) => r.id)))\n  const toggleOne = (id) => {\n    const next = new Set(selected)\n    \/\/ eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-expressions\n    next.has(id) ? next.delete(id) : next.add(id)\n    onSelect(next)\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"overflow-x-auto rounded-card border border-line bg-surface\">\n      <table className=\"w-full min-w-[900px] text-sm\">\n        {\/* Sticky header: these tables get long, and a scrolled-away header\n            turns a dense grid into unlabelled noise. *\/}\n        <thead className=\"sticky top-0 z-10 bg-surface-2\/95 backdrop-blur\">\n          <tr className=\"border-b border-line text-left text-tx-3\">\n            <th className=\"w-10 px-3 py-3\">\n              <input\n                type=\"checkbox\"\n                checked={allSelected}\n                onChange={toggleAll}\n                aria-label=\"Select all leads on this page\"\n                className=\"accent-brand\"\n              \/>\n            <\/th>\n            {cols.map((c) => (\n              <SortableHeader key={c.key} col={c} sort={sort} onSort={onSort} \/>\n            ))}\n          <\/tr>\n        <\/thead>\n        <tbody>\n          {isLoading ? (\n            <SkeletonRows cols={cols.length + 1} \/>\n          ) : rows.length === 0 ? (\n            <tr>\n              <td colSpan={cols.length + 1} className=\"px-4 py-16 text-center\">\n                <Inbox size={26} className=\"mx-auto mb-3 text-tx-3\" \/>\n                <div className=\"text-tx-2\">\n                  {hasFilters ? 'No leads match these filters.' : 'No leads yet.'}\n                <\/div>\n                <div className=\"mt-1 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n                  {hasFilters\n                    ? 'Try clearing a filter or widening the date range.'\n                    : 'Website leads arrive here automatically. Use Add Lead for the rest.'}\n                <\/div>\n              <\/td>\n            <\/tr>\n          ) : (\n            rows.map((lead) => (\n              <tr\n                key={lead.id}\n                onClick={() => onOpen(lead)}\n                className=\"cursor-pointer border-b border-line\/60 transition last:border-0 hover:bg-surface-2\"\n              >\n                <td className=\"px-3 py-3\" onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>\n                  <input\n                    type=\"checkbox\"\n                    checked={selected.has(lead.id)}\n                    onChange={() => toggleOne(lead.id)}\n                    aria-label={`Select ${lead.business_name}`}\n                    className=\"accent-brand\"\n                  \/>\n                <\/td>\n                {cols.map((c) => (\n                  <td key={c.key} className=\"px-4 py-3\">\n                    <Cell col={c.key} lead={lead} choices={choices} \/>\n                  <\/td>\n                ))}\n              <\/tr>\n            ))\n          )}\n        <\/tbody>\n      <\/table>\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction SortableHeader({ col, sort, onSort }) {\n  if (!col.sort) {\n    return <th className=\"whitespace-nowrap px-4 py-3 text-xs font-medium\">{col.label}<\/th>\n  }\n\n  const active = sort === col.sort || sort === `-${col.sort}`\n  const desc = sort === `-${col.sort}`\n  const Icon = !active ? ChevronsUpDown : desc ? ArrowDown : ArrowUp\n\n  return (\n    <th className=\"whitespace-nowrap px-4 py-3 text-xs font-medium\">\n      <button\n        onClick={() => onSort(active && desc ? col.sort : `-${col.sort}`)}\n        className={`flex items-center gap-1 transition hover:text-tx ${active ? 'text-brand' : ''}`}\n      >\n        {col.label}\n        <Icon size={12} className={active ? '' : 'opacity-40'} \/>\n      <\/button>\n    <\/th>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction Cell({ col, lead, choices }) {\n  switch (col) {\n    case 'business':\n      return (\n        <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n          {\/* The one place lead type earns space in the default view: a small\n              mark, not a column, since it is context rather than a value. *\/}\n          {lead.lead_type === 'website' ? (\n            <Globe size={13} className=\"shrink-0 text-info\" aria-label=\"Website lead\" \/>\n          ) : (\n            <UserPlus size={13} className=\"shrink-0 text-tx-3\" aria-label=\"Manual lead\" \/>\n          )}\n          <span className=\"font-medium text-tx\">{lead.business_name}<\/span>\n        <\/div>\n      )\n    case 'owner':\n      return <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{lead.name || '—'}<\/span>\n    case 'phone':\n      return (\n        <a\n          href={`tel:${lead.phone}`}\n          onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}\n          className=\"font-num text-tx-2 hover:text-brand\"\n        >\n          {lead.phone || '—'}\n        <\/a>\n      )\n    case 'area':\n      return <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{lead.area || '—'}<\/span>\n    case 'category':\n      return <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{labelFor(choices, KIND.CATEGORY, lead.category)}<\/span>\n    case 'assigned_sales':\n      return lead.assigned_sales ? (\n        <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{lead.assigned_sales.name || lead.assigned_sales.email}<\/span>\n      ) : (\n        <span className=\"text-xs text-tx-3\">Unassigned<\/span>\n      )\n    case 'priority':\n      return (\n        <Badge tone={PRIORITY_TONE[lead.priority] ?? 'neutral'}>\n          {labelFor(choices, KIND.PRIORITY, lead.priority)}\n        <\/Badge>\n      )\n    case 'status':\n      return <StatusBadge lead={lead} choices={choices} \/>\n    case 'temperature':\n      return (\n        <Badge tone={TEMPERATURE_TONE[lead.temperature] ?? 'neutral'}>\n          {labelFor(choices, KIND.TEMPERATURE, lead.temperature)}\n        <\/Badge>\n      )\n    case 'lead_score':\n      return <ScoreBar score={lead.lead_score} \/>\n    case 'lead_type':\n      return <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{titleCase(lead.lead_type)}<\/span>\n    case 'source':\n      return <span className=\"text-tx-2\">{labelFor(choices, KIND.SOURCE, lead.source)}<\/span>\n    case 'next_follow_up_at':\n      return <FollowUp lead={lead} \/>\n    case 'last_activity':\n      return (\n        <span className=\"block max-w-[220px] truncate text-tx-3\" title={lead.last_activity}>\n          {lead.last_activity || '—'}\n        <\/span>\n      )\n    case 'created_at':\n      return <span className=\"whitespace-nowrap text-tx-3\">{shortDate(lead.created_at)}<\/span>\n    default:\n      return null\n  }\n}\n\n\/\/ The status badge takes its colour from the admin's own CRM configuration, so\n\/\/ a re-coloured status re-colours here without a deploy. Falls back to the\n\/\/ neutral Badge when no colour is set — most statuses have none, deliberately.\nfunction StatusBadge({ lead, choices }) {\n  const color = colorFor(choices, KIND.STATUS, lead.status)\n  const label = labelFor(choices, KIND.STATUS, lead.status)\n\n  if (!color) return <Badge>{label}<\/Badge>\n  return (\n    <span\n      className=\"inline-flex items-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold\"\n      style={{ backgroundColor: `${color}22`, color }}\n    >\n      {label}\n    <\/span>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction ScoreBar({ score = 0 }) {\n  const tone = scoreTone(score)\n  return (\n    <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n      <div className=\"h-1.5 w-14 overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-surface-3\">\n        <div className={`h-full rounded-full ${tone.bar}`} style={{ width: `${score}%` }} \/>\n      <\/div>\n      <span className={`font-num text-xs ${tone.text}`}>{score}<\/span>\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\n\/\/ A follow-up in the past is the table's one piece of urgency, so it is the one\n\/\/ thing allowed to shout.\nfunction FollowUp({ lead }) {\n  if (!lead.next_follow_up_at) return <span className=\"text-tx-3\">—<\/span>\n\n  const overdue = new Date(lead.next_follow_up_at) < new Date()\n  return (\n    <span className={`whitespace-nowrap text-xs ${overdue ?
