An import is a batch of independent\n    facts, and rolling back three hundred good leads because row 301 has a\n    malformed email would be obviously wrong. Each row is its own transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n    validate_mapping(mapping)\n\n    created = 0\n    skipped: list[dict] = []\n    failed: list[dict] = []\n\n    for index, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):  # row 1 is the header, as a human counts\n        fields = _row_to_fields(row, mapping)\n\n        if not fields.get(\"business_name\") or not fields.get(\"phone\"):\n            failed.append({\"row\": index, \"reason\": \"Missing business name or phone.\"})\n            continue\n\n        if skip_duplicates:\n            existing = crm_service.find_duplicates(\n                phone=fields.get(\"phone\", \"\"),\n                email=fields.get(\"email\", \"\"),\n                business_name=fields.get(\"business_name\", \"\"),\n            ).first()\n            if existing is not None:\n                skipped.append(\n                    {\n                        \"row\": index,\n                        \"business_name\": fields[\"business_name\"],\n                        \"reason\": \"Already in the pipeline.\",\n                        \"lead_id\": str(existing.id),\n                    }\n                )\n                continue\n\n        try:\n            with transaction.atomic():\n                crm_service.create_manual_lead(\n                    actor=actor,\n                    source=source,\n                    assigned_sales=assigned_sales,\n                    **fields,\n                )\n            created += 1\n        except Exception as exc:  # setFile(f)\n    setErr('')\n    try {\n      const data = await runPreview.mutateAsync(f)\n      setPreview(data)\n      setMapping(data.suggested_mapping)\n      setStep('map')\n    } catch (e) {\n      setErr(normalizeError(e).message)\n    }\n  }\n\n  async function submit() {\n    setErr('')\n    try {\n      const summary = await runImport.mutateAsync({\n        file,\n        mapping,\n        source,\n        assigned_sales: assigned,\n        skip_duplicates: skipDuplicates,\n      })\n      setResult(summary)\n      setStep('result')\n    } catch (e) {\n      setErr(normalizeError(e).message)\n    }\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-start justify-center overflow-y-auto bg-black\/50 p-4\">\n      <div className=\"my-8 []}\n            choices={choices}\n            onBack={() => setStep('upload')}\n            onSubmit={submit}\n            busy={runImport.isPending}\n          \/>\n        )}\n\n        {step === 'result' && result && (\n          <ResultStep\n            result={result}\n            onClose={() => {\n              onDone?.(result)\n              onClose()\n            }}\n          \/>\n        )}\n      <\/div>\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction Stepper({ step }) {\n  const at = STEPS.indexOf(step)\n  const labels = ['Upload file', 'Map columns', 'Done']\n  return (\n    <div className=\"mb-5 flex items-center gap-2\">\n      {labels.map((label, i) => (\n        <div key={label} className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n          <div\n            className={`flex h-6 w-6 items-center justify-center rounded-full text-xs font-semibold ${\n              i < at\n                ? 'bg-brand text-white'\n                  : 'bg-surface-2 text-tx-3'\n            }`}\n          >\n            {i < at ? <Check size={13} \/> : i + 1}\n          <\/div>\n          <span className={`text-xs ${i === at ? 'text-tx' : 'text-tx-3'}`}>{label}<\/span>\n          {i < labels.length - 1 && <div className=\"mx-1 h-px w-6 bg-line\" \/>}\n        <\/div>\n      ))}\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction UploadStep({ onPick, busy }) {\n  const input = useRef(null)\n  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        onClick={() => input.current?.click()}\n        onDragOver={(e) => {\n          e.preventDefault()\n          setDragging(true)\n        }}\n        onDragLeave={() => setDragging(false)}\n        onDrop={(e) => {\n          e.preventDefault()\n          setDragging(false)\n          onPick(e.dataTransfer.files?.[0])\n        }}\n        className={`flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-card border-2 border-dashed p-10 transition ${\n          dragging ? 'border-brand bg-brand-bg\/30' : 'border-line hover:border-brand\/50'\n        }`}\n      >\n        {busy ? (\n          <Loader2 size={28} className=\"animate-spin text-brand\" \/>\n        ) : (\n          <Upload size={28} className=\"text-tx-3\" \/>\n        )}\n        <div className=\"text-center\">\n          <div className=\"text-sm font-medium text-tx\">\n            {busy ? 'Reading your file…' : 'Drop a file here, or click to choose'}\n          <\/div>\n          <div className=\"mt-1 text-xs text-tx-3\">CSV or Excel (.xlsx) · up to 5 MB<\/div>\n        <\/div>\n      <\/button>\n\n      <input\n        ref={input}\n        type=\"file\"\n        accept=\".csv,.xlsx,.xlsm,text\/csv\"\n        onChange={(e) => onPick(e.target.files?.[0])}\n        className=\"hidden\"\n      \/>\n\n      <div className=\"mt-4 rounded-ctl border border-line bg-bg p-3 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n        Your file needs a header row with at least a <b className=\"text-tx-2\">business name<\/b> and\n        a <b className=\"text-tx-2\">phone<\/b> column. Everything else is optional and you map it on\n        the next step.\n      <\/div>\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction MapStep({\n  preview,\n  mapping,\n  setMapping,\n  source,\n  setSource,\n  assigned,\n  setAssigned,\n  skipDuplicates,\n  setSkipDuplicates,\n  salesUsers,\n  choices,\n  onBack,\n  onSubmit,\n  busy,\n}) {\n  const setColumn = (column, field) => {\n    const next = { ...mapping }\n    if (field) {\n      \/\/ One field per column: clear any other column that already claimed it,\n      \/\/ so two columns can't both map to phone and silently fight.\n      for (const [c, f] of Object.entries(next)) if (f === field && c !== column) delete next[c]\n      next[column] = field\n    } else {\n      delete next[column]\n    }\n    setMapping(next)\n  }\n\n  const mappedFields = new Set(Object.values(mapping))\n  const missingRequired = preview.fields\n    .filter((f) => f.required && !mappedFields.has(f.field))\n    .map((f) => f.label)\n  const canImport = missingRequired.length === 0 && !busy\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div className=\"mb-3 flex items-center justify-between text-sm\">\n        <span className=\"text-tx-2\">\n          {preview.total_rows.toLocaleString()} row{preview.total_rows === 1 ? '' : 's'} found\n        <\/span>\n        {preview.existing_matches > 0 && (\n          <span className=\"text-warn\">\n            {preview.existing_matches} already in the pipeline\n          <\/span>\n        )}\n      <\/div>\n\n      {\/* Map each column to a field. The sample value under each column is what\n          makes a wrong guess obvious before it is applied. *\/}\n      <div className=\"max-h-64 overflow-y-auto rounded-ctl border border-line\">\n        <table className=\"w-full text-sm\">\n          <thead className=\"sticky top-0 bg-surface-2 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n            <tr>\n              <th className=\"px-3 py-2 text-left font-medium\">Your column<\/th>\n              <th className=\"px-3 py-2 text-left font-medium\">Sample<\/th>\n              <th className=\"px-3 py-2 text-left font-medium\">Imports as<\/th>\n            <\/tr>\n          <\/thead>\n          <tbody>\n            {preview.columns.map((column) => (\n              <tr key={column} className=\"border-t border-line\/60\">\n                <td className=\"px-3 py-2 font-medium text-tx\">{column}<\/td>\n                <td className=\"max-w-[160px] truncate px-3 py-2 text-tx-3\">\n                  {preview.sample[0]?.[column] || '—'}\n                <\/td>\n                <td className=\"px-3 py-2\">\n                  <select\n                    value={mapping[column] || ''}\n                    onChange={(e) => setColumn(column, e.target.value)}\n                    className=\"w-full rounded-ctl border border-line bg-bg px-2 py-1 text-sm text-tx focus:border-brand focus:outline-none\"\n                  >\n                    <option value=\"\">— Don’t import —<\/option>\n                    {preview.fields.map((f) => (\n                      <option key={f.field} value={f.field}>\n                        {f.label}\n                        {f.required ? ' *' : ''}\n                      <\/option>\n                    ))}\n                  <\/select>\n                <\/td>\n              <\/tr>\n            ))}\n          <\/tbody>\n        <\/table>\n      <\/div>\n\n      {missingRequired.length > 0 && (\n        <div className=\"mt-3 flex items-center gap-2 text-xs text-warn\">\n          <AlertTriangle size={13} \/>\n          Map a column to {missingRequired.join(' and ')} — a lead needs {missingRequired.length > 1 ? 'them' : 'it'}.\n        <\/div>\n      )}\n\n      <div className=\"mt-4 grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 border-t border-line pt-4 sm:grid-cols-2\">\n        <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n          Source for all imported leads\n          <select\n            value={source}\n            onChange={(e) => setSource(e.target.value)}\n            className=\"rounded-ctl border border-line bg-bg px-3 py-2 text-sm text-tx focus:border-brand focus:outline-none\"\n          >\n            {optionsFor(choices, KIND.SOURCE).map((c) => (\n              <option key={c.slug} value={c.slug}>\n                {c.label}\n              <\/option>\n            ))}\n          <\/select>\n        <\/label>\n\n        <label className=\"flex flex-col gap-1 text-xs text-tx-3\">\n          Assign all to\n          <select\n            value={assigned}\n            onChange={(e) => setAssigned(e.target.value)}\n            className=\"rounded-ctl border border-line bg-bg px-3 value={a.id}>\n                {a.name || a.email}\n              <\/option>\n            ))}\n          <\/select>\n        <\/label>\n      <\/div>\n\n      <label className=\"mt-3 flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-tx-2\">\n        <input\n          type=\"checkbox\"\n          checked={skipDuplicates}\n          onChange={(e) => setSkipDuplicates(e.target.checked)}\n          className=\"accent-brand\"\n        \/>\n        Skip rows that already exist (by phone, email or business name)\n      <\/label>\n\n      <div className=\"mt-5 flex justify-between\">\n        <button\n          onClick={onBack}\n          className=\"rounded-ctl border border-line px-4 py-2 text-sm text-tx-2 hover:text-tx\"\n        >\n          Back\n        <\/button>\n        <button\n          onClick={onSubmit}\n          disabled={!canImport}\n          className=\"flex items-center gap-2 rounded-ctl bg-brand px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white hover:bg-brand-d disabled:opacity-50\"\n        >\n          {busy ? <Loader2 size={14} className=\"animate-spin\" \/> : <ArrowRight size={14} \/>}\n          Import {preview.total_rows.toLocaleString()} row{preview.total_rows === 1 ? '' : 's'}\n        <\/button>\n      <\/div>\n    <\/div>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction ResultStep({ result, onClose }) {\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div className=\"mb-4 flex flex-col items-center gap-2 py-4\">\n        <div className=\"flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-success\/20\">\n          <Check size={24} className=\"text-success\" \/>\n        <\/div>\n        <div className=\"text-lg font-semibold text-tx\">Import complete<\/div>\n      <\/div>\n\n      <div className=\"grid grid-cols-3 gap-3\">\n        <Tally label=\"Created\" value={result.created} tone=\"text-success\" \/>\n        <Tally label=\"Skipped\" value={result.skipped} tone=\"text-warn\" \/>\n        <Tally label=\"Failed\" value={result.failed} tone={result.failed ? ## 945 · Claude

CSV/Excel import is done, verified end-to-end in the browser, and all gates are green.

**The wizard** is three steps — Upload → Map → Result. Drop a file, it previews what it found and proposes a column mapping, you confirm, and it imports with a summary of created/skipped/failed. I drove it in a browser with a deliberately messy CSV (semicolon-delimited, Arabic business names, a bad email, a blank line) and it handled all of it: **5 created, 0 failed**, columns auto-mapped, phones stored as text not floats, the bad email dropped while keeping the lead, categories matched to your configured choices, and the blank line skipped silently.

**Three design decisions worth flagging:**

1. **It's a two-call flow — preview then import — because nothing gets written until a human confirms the mapping.** A spreadsheet imported blind puts phone numbers in the area field of four hundred leads and nobody notices until they call one. The preview also tells you "40 of these 200 are already in the pipeline" before you commit.

2. **Column matching is exact-alias only, never fuzzy.** A near-match that quietly guesses wrong is worse than leaving a column unmapped and making someone pick — the first mistake is invisible, the second isn't. Unrecognized columns just show "Don't import".

3. **Each row is its own transaction, not atomic across the batch.** Rolling back 300 good leads because row 301 has a malformed email would be obviously wrong. Bad rows are named in the summary; imported leads go through the same `create_manual_lead` path as typed ones, so they get identical provenance, timeline, and score.

**One new dependency:** `openpyxl` for `.xlsx`, added to `requirements.txt` with a note on why (CSV is stdlib; Sales gets handed Excel files and telling them to re-save each one is how a feature goes unused). Workbooks open read-only + data-only, so formulas are never evaluated. The old binary `.xls` is deliberately refused with advice to re-save.

**Verification:** 942 backend tests (34 new for import), 37 frontend tests, all seven CI gates clean, browser pass with zero console errors. Test data and artifacts cleaned up.

That leaves **Merge Duplicates** — the last item, and the smallest, since the Open and Create-anyway paths already cover most of the duplicate story. Want me to finish with that?

```
208	def find_duplicates(*, phone: str = "", email: str = "", business_name: str = "", exclude_id=None):
209	    """Leads that may already be this one.
210	
211	    Phone and email match exactly; business name matches case-insensitively and
212	    whole, not as a substring — "Bloom" must not collide with every café in
213	    Cairo whose name contains it. Deliberately advisory: the caller decides
214	    whether a hit blocks, merges, or is ignored, because a shop with two
215	    branches legitimately has two leads on one phone number.
216	    """
217	    probes = Q()
218	    if phone:
219	        probes |= Q(phone=phone)
220	    if email:
221	        probes |= Q(email__iexact=email)
222	    if business_name:
223	        probes |= Q(business_name__iexact=business_name.strip())

225	        return Lead.objects.none()
226	
227	    matches = Lead.objects.filter(probes)
228	    if exclude_id:

230	    return matches.select_related("assigned_sales")
```

```json
  "new_string" : "    matches = Lead.objects.filter(probes)\n    if exclude_id:\n        matches = matches.exclude(pk=exclude_id)\n    return matches.select_related(\"assigned_sales\")\n\n\nclass MergeError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A merge that cannot proceed, explained for a salesperson.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str):\n        self.code = code\n        self.message = message\n        super().__init__(message)\n\n\n# Fields whose values are worth carrying over from the absorbed lead. CRM state\n# (status, priority, score, assignment) is deliberately absent: the survivor is\n# the record being kept, and its pipeline position is the true one — pulling the\n# absorbed lead's status over could drag a \"Customer\" back to \"New Lead\". Only\n# business facts fill gaps.\n_MERGE_FILL_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (\n    \"name\",\n    \"whatsapp\",\n    \"email\",\n    \"instagram\",\n    \"facebook\",\n    \"website\",\n    \"google_maps_url\",\n    \"logo_url\",\n    \"area\",\n    \"category\",\n    \"address\",\n    \"expected_plan\",\n    \"expected_revenue\",\n)\n\n\n@transaction.atomic\ndef merge_leads(*, survivor: Lead, absorbed: Lead, actor: AdminUser) -> Lead:\n    \"\"\"Fold ``absorbed`` into ``survivor`` and delete it. Returns the survivor.\n\n    The survivor wins every conflict: a field it already has is never\n    overwritten, and its pipeline position stands. The absorbed lead only fills\n    the survivor's blanks and hands over its history — its calls and its\n    timeline move across, so nothing that happened is lost when the row goes.\n\n    Refused when the absorbed lead has been converted: it is linked to a live\n    merchant, and deleting it would strand that merchant's origin. Merge the\n    other direction, or don't.\n    \"\"\"\n    if survivor.pk == absorbed.pk:\n        raise MergeError(\"SAME_LEAD\", \"A lead cannot be merged into itself.\")\n    if absorbed.is_converted:\n        raise MergeError(\n            \"ABSORBED_CONVERTED\",\n            f\"{absorbed.business_name} is already a merchant — merge the other lead into it \"\n            \"instead, so the merchant link is kept.\",\n        )\n\n    # Reparent history before touching the survivor's fields, so a failure here\n    # rolls the whole thing back rather than leaving orphaned calls.\n    absorbed.calls.update(lead=survivor)\n    absorbed.activities.update(lead=survivor)\n\n    filled = []\n    for field in _MERGE_FILL_FIELDS:\n        if not getattr(survivor, field) and getattr(absorbed, field):\n            setattr(survivor, field, getattr(absorbed, field))\n            filled.append(field)\n\n    # Merge free-text notes rather than letting one win — a note is the one field\n    # where both leads' content is worth keeping verbatim.\n    if absorbed.notes and absorbed.notes not in survivor.notes:\n        survivor.notes = f\"{survivor.notes}\\n\\n{absorbed.notes}\".strip()\n        filled.append(\"notes\")\n\n    if filled:\n        survivor.save()\n\n    absorbed_label = f\"{absorbed.business_name} · {absorbed.phone}\"\n    absorbed.delete()  # cascades nothing now — its calls and activities moved\n\n    log_activity(\n        survivor,\n        crm.ActivityKind.DUPLICATE_MERGED,\n        \"Duplicate Merged\",\n        description=f\"Merged in {absorbed_label}.\",\n        actor=actor,\n    )\n    return survivor",
```

## 1052 · Claude

Merge Duplicates is done and verified in the browser — **that completes the entire Lead Management CRM.** All five stages you laid out are built.

**Merge, specifically:** from a lead's detail page, the merge button lists that lead's likely duplicates and folds a chosen one in. I watched it work end-to-end: the survivor kept its "Interested / High / Hot" position, absorbed the other lead's email, Instagram, area, notes, and its logged call, put "Duplicate Merged" on the timeline, and deleted the absorbed row with zero orphans left behind.

**The one design decision that makes merge safe:** the lead on screen is always the *survivor* — you merge *into* the record you're keeping. That direction is deliberate. The survivor's status, priority, and already-filled fields are never touched; only its blanks get filled. So a merge can't accidentally drag a qualified lead back to "New Lead", which the wrong direction easily could. A converted lead can't be absorbed (it's a live merchant — deleting it would strand that link), and the modal shows converted duplicates greyed-out with the reason rather than hiding them.

---

**Where the whole build stands.** The Leads page is now a complete CRM, and every stage was verified in a real browser, not just in tests:

| Import + Merge | CSV/Excel import with column mapping; duplicate merge |

```
========== stampn-ops/README.md ==========
# Stampn Ops — isolated feature workspace

This directory is the reviewable, reversible workspace for **Stampn Ops**.  It
does not alter the running applications.  `PROMOTION_MANIFEST.md` lists the
exact destination of every file when the feature is approved for integration.

## Security model

Stampn Ops is an internal control plane, not a tenant feature:

- every dashboard and settings endpoint is `SUPER_ADMIN` only;
- the Django application never receives the Docker socket, host filesystem, or
  shell access;
- a small collector is the sole component with read-only host mounts and the
  Docker socket.  It has no public port and accepts requests only from the
  Docker network with a high-entropy bearer token;
- Telegram tokens are encrypted at rest by the Django application and are
  never returned by its API after saving;
- snapshots are bounded, redacted, cached, and pull-only.  Logs are limited to
  a short, redacted tail so Ops cannot become a secret-exfiltration endpoint.

## Delivery order

1. Build and test the collector locally against a Docker host.
2. Promote the backend models, services, endpoints, tasks, and migration.
3. Promote the Admin SPA feature and Super Admin-only navigation entry.

5. Run the full `dev` CI gate and manually validate from a Super Admin session.
6. Only after approval, merge `dev` into `prod`; production is never deployed
   directly from this workspace.

The collector reports facts. The Django service owns alert thresholds, health
score calculation, persistence, audit logging, Telegram delivery, quiet hours,
and authorization. This split keeps host privileges out of customer-facing
application code.
```

```
# Staged WhatsApp Cloud API authentication

This is isolated source only; it is not installed or routed in Stampn yet.

## Identity rule

An OTP proves control of a phone number; it does **not** identify a Stampn
account by itself. `WhatsAppIdentity` maps a normalized, previously verified
phone to one Django user. `link_phone(user, phone)` is called from the future
signup/profile verification flow. Login OTP returns JWT only for that mapped,
active user. This prevents account creation or account takeover from an unknown
number.
```

```
===== utils.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import re
from django.conf import settings
from rest_framework.exceptions import ValidationError

_E164 = re.compile(r"^\+[1-9]\d{7,14}$")


def normalize_phone(value: str) -> str:
    phone = value.strip().replace(" ", "").replace("-", "")
    if phone.startswith("00"):
        phone = "+" + phone[2:]
    if not _E164.fullmatch(phone):
        raise ValidationError({"phone": "Use an E.164 number, e.g. +2010XXXXXXX."})
    return phone


def phone_key(phone: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(phone.encode()).hexdigest()


def otp_digest(phone: str, otp: str) -> str:
    return hmac.new(settings.SECRET_KEY.encode(), f"{phone}:{otp}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def mask_phone(phone: str) -> str:
    return f"{phone[:3]}••••{phone[-3:]}" if len(phone) > 6 else "••••"
```

```
from __future__ import annotations
import secrets
import time
from django.core.cache import cache
from rest_framework_simplejwt.tokens import RefreshToken
from .client import WhatsAppClient
from .exceptions import OTPInvalid, OTPRateLimited
from .models import WhatsAppIdentity, WhatsAppMessageLog
from .utils import mask_phone, normalize_phone, otp_digest, phone_key

OTP_TTL = 300

class OTPService:
    def __init__(self, client: WhatsAppClient | None = None): self.client = client or WhatsAppClient()
    def _key(self, prefix: str, phone: str) -> str: return f"wa_otp:{prefix}:{phone_key(phone)}"
    def generate_otp(self, phone: str) -> str: return f"{secrets.randbelow(1_000_000):06d}"
    def _check_limits(self, phone: str) -> None:
        if cache.get(self._key("cooldown", phone)):
            raise OTPRateLimited("Please wait before requesting another code.")
        hourly = self._key("hour")
        cache.add(hourly, 0, 3600)
        if int(cache.get(hourly) or 0) >= 5: raise OTPRateLimited("Maximum verification messages reached for this hour.")
    def send_otp(self, phone: str) -> None:
        phone = normalize_phone(phone); self._check_limits(phone); otp = self.generate_otp(phone)
        result = self.client.send_template(phone, "stampn_login", "en", [otp])
        message_id = (result.get("messages") or [{}])[0].get("id", "")
        WhatsAppMessageLog.objects.create(message_id=message_id, phone_masked=mask_phone(phone), meta_response=result)
        cache.set(self._key("code", phone), {"digest": otp_digest(phone, otp), "attempts": 0, "issued": time.monotonic()}, OTP_TTL)
        cache.set(self._key("cooldown", phone), True, 60); cache.incr(self._key("hour", phone))
    def verify_otp(self, phone: str, otp: str):
        phone = normalize_phone(phone); key = self._key("code", phone); record = cache.get(key)
        if not record: raise OTPInvalid()
        remaining = int(OTP_TTL - (time.monotonic() - record.get("issued", 0)))
        if remaining <= 0: cache.delete(key); raise OTPInvalid()
        if int(record.get("attempts", 0)) >= 3: cache.delete(key); raise OTPRateLimited("Too many invalid code attempts.")
        import hmac
        if not hmac.compare_digest(record["digest"], otp_digest(phone, otp)):
            record["attempts"] += 1; cache.set(key, record, remaining); raise OTPInvalid()
        cache.delete(key)
        identity = WhatsAppIdentity.objects.select_related("user").filter(phone=phone).first()
        if not identity or not identity.user.is_active: raise OTPInvalid("No active account is linked to this phone.")
        refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(identity.user)
        return {"access": str(refresh.access_token), "refresh": str(refresh)}

def link_phone(user, phone: str) -> WhatsAppIdentity:
    phone = normalize_phone(phone)
    identity, _ = WhatsAppIdentity.objects.update_or_create(user=user, defaults={"phone": phone})
    return identity
```

```
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib, hmac, logging
from django.conf import settings
from .models import WhatsAppMessageLog

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def valid_signature(raw: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(settings.WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET.encode(), raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return bool(settings.WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET) and hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)

def process(payload: dict) -> None:
    for entry in payload.get("entry", []):
        for change in entry.get("changes", []):
            for status in change.get("value", {}).get("statuses", []):
                message_id = status.get("id", "")
                if not message_id: continue
                WhatsAppMessageLog.objects.filter(message_id=message_id).update(status=status.get("status", "unknown"), meta_response=status, error=(status.get("errors") or [{}])[0].get("title", ""))

===== client.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any
import httpx
from django.conf import settings

from .exceptions import WhatsAppProviderError
from .utils import mask_phone

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class WhatsAppClient:
    """Only Meta Graph API transport; policy and OTP logic stay in services."""
    def __init__(self, *, token: str | None = None, phone_number_id: str | None = None, transport: httpx.Client | None = None):
        self.token = token if token is not None else settings.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN
        self.phone_number_id = phone_number_id if phone_number_id is not None else settings.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
        self.version = settings.WHATSAPP_API_VERSION
        self.http = transport or httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(8.0, connect=3.0))

    @property
    def url(self) -> str:
        return f"https://graph.facebook.com/{self.version}/{self.phone_number_id}/messages"

    def _post(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        for attempt in range(3):
            try:
                response = self.http.post(self.url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"}, json=payload)
                if response.status_code < 500:
                    response.raise_for_status(); return response.json()
            except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
                if attempt == 2:
                    logger.warning("whatsapp_api_failed error=%s", str(exc)[:160])
                    raise WhatsAppProviderError() from exc
        raise WhatsAppProviderError()

    def send_template(self, to: str, template_name: str, language: str, parameters: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        logger.info("whatsapp_template_send phone=%s template=%s", mask_phone(to), template_name)
        return self._post({"messaging_product": "whatsapp", "to": to, "type": "template", "template": {"name": template_name, "language": {"code": language}, "components": [{"type": "body", "parameters": [{"type": "text", "text": p} for p in parameters]}]}})

    def send_text(self, to: str, message: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self._post({"messaging_product": "whatsapp", "to": to, "type": "text", "text": {"body": message}})

    def mark_as_read(self, message_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self._post({"messaging_product": "whatsapp", "status": "read", "message_id": message_id})
```

```
from __future__ import annotations
from django.conf import settings
from rest_framework.permissions import AllowAny
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.views import APIView
from .serializers import SendOTPSerializer, VerifyOTPSerializer
from .services import OTPService
from .webhook import process, valid_signature

class SendWhatsAppOTPView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [AllowAny]; throttle_scope = "auth"
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        body = SendOTPSerializer(data=request.data); body.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        OTPService().send_otp(body.validated_data["phone"])
        return Response({"success": True})

class VerifyWhatsAppOTPView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [AllowAny]; throttle_scope = "auth"
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        body = VerifyOTPSerializer(data=request.data); body.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        return Response(OTPService().verify_otp(**body.validated_data))

class WhatsAppWebhookView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [AllowAny]; authentication_classes = []
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        if request.query_params.get("hub.mode") == "subscribe" and request.query_params.get("hub.verify_token") == settings.WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN:
            return Response(request.query_params.get("hub.challenge", ""), content_type="text/plain")
        return Response(status=403)
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        if not valid_signature(request.body, request.headers.get("X-Hub-Signature-256", "")): return Response(status=401)
        process(request.data); return Response(status=200)

from common.errors import DomainError, ErrorCode


class WhatsAppProviderError(DomainError):
    status_code = 502
    error_code = ErrorCode.SERVER_ERROR
    default_detail = "Authentication message could not be sent."


class OTPInvalid(DomainError):
    status_code = 400
    error_code = ErrorCode.VALIDATION_ERROR
    default_detail = "The verification code is invalid or expired."


class OTPRateLimited(DomainError):
    status_code = 429
    error_code = ErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED
    default_detail = "Too many verification requests. Please try again later."

class VerifyOTPSerializer(SendOTPSerializer):
```

```
"""Persistent, platform-owned Ops data. No merchant data belongs here."""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.db import models

from core.models import TimeStampedModel, UUIDModel


class OpsConfiguration(TimeStampedModel):
    """Singleton encrypted notification settings and configurable thresholds."""

    singleton = models.BooleanField(default=True, unique=True, editable=False)
    telegram_bot_token_encrypted = models.BinaryField(blank=True, editable=False)
    telegram_chat_id = models.CharField(max_length=80, blank=True)
    notifications_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    hourly_reports_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    critical_alerts_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    warning_alerts_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    deployment_alerts_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    backup_alerts_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    ssl_alerts_enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    quiet_hours_start = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    quiet_hours_end = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    thresholds = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)

    @classmethod
    def defaults(cls) -> dict[str, float]:
        return {"cpu_warning": 80, "cpu_critical": 90, "ram_warning": 80,
                "ram_critical": 90, "disk_warning": 80, "disk_critical": 90,
                "load_warning": 2.0, "response_time_warning_ms": 500,
                "error_rate_warning": 5, "queue_size_warning": 100,
                "failed_jobs_warning": 10}

    @classmethod
    def current(cls) -> "OpsConfiguration":
        obj, _ = cls.objects.get_or_create(singleton=True, defaults={"thresholds": cls.defaults()})
        if not obj.thresholds:
            obj.thresholds = cls.defaults()
            obj.save(update_fields=["thresholds", "updated_at"])
        return obj


class OpsSnapshot(UUIDModel):
    observed_at = models.DateTimeField(db_index=True)
    health_score = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField()
    status = models.CharField(max_length=16)
    payload = models.JSONField()

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["-observed_at"]


class OpsAlert(UUIDModel, TimeStampedModel):
    fingerprint = models.CharField(max_length=160, unique=True)
    severity = models.CharField(max_length=12)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=12, default="open")
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    detail = models.TextField(blank=True)
    first_seen_at = models.DateTimeField()
    last_seen_at = models.DateTimeField()
    resolved_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    occurrences = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=1)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["-last_seen_at"]


class OpsDeployment(UUIDModel, TimeStampedModel):
    commit_sha = models.CharField(max_length=64, db_index=True)
    branch = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    message = models.CharField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    deployed_by = models.CharField(max_length=180, blank=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=16)
    started_at = models.DateTimeField()
    finished_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    duration_seconds = models.PositiveIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)

from __future__ import annotations

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
from django.conf import settings
from django.utils import timezone
from rest_framework.request import Request
from rest_framework.response import Response

from console import audit
from console.enums import AdminRole
from console.permissions import AdminAPIView

from .models import OpsAlert, OpsConfiguration
from .serializers import OpsSettingsSerializer
from .services import dashboard
from .telegram import send


class SuperAdminOpsView(AdminAPIView):
    allowed_roles = {AdminRole.SUPER_ADMIN}


class OpsDashboardView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        audit.record(request, "stampn_ops.dashboard_read", target_type="ops")
        return Response(dashboard())


class OpsRefreshView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        result = dashboard(refresh=True)
        audit.record(request, "stampn_ops.refresh", target_type="ops")
        return Response(result)


class OpsAlertListView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        status = request.query_params.get("status", "open")
        rows = OpsAlert.objects.filter(status=status)[:100]
        return Response({"results": [{"id": str(x.id), "severity": x.severity, "status": x.status, "title": x.title, "detail": x.detail, "first_seen_at": x.first_seen_at, "last_seen_at": x.last_seen_at, "occurrences": x.occurrences} for x in rows]})


class OpsSettingsView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        return Response(OpsSettingsSerializer(OpsConfiguration.current()).data)

    def patch(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        config = OpsConfiguration.current(); body = OpsSettingsSerializer(config, data=request.data, partial=True); body.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        token = body.validated_data.pop("telegram_bot_token", None)
        config = body.save()
        if token:
            config.telegram_bot_token_encrypted = Fernet(settings.OPS_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.encode()).encrypt(token.encode())
            config.save(update_fields=["telegram_bot_token_encrypted", "updated_at"])
        audit.record(request, "stampn_ops.settings_update", target_type="ops")
        return Response(OpsSettingsSerializer(config).data)


class TelegramTestView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    def post(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        ok = send(OpsConfiguration.current(), "✅ Stampn Ops test notification")
        audit.record(request, "stampn_ops.telegram_test", target_type="ops", metadata={"sent": ok})
        return Response({"sent": ok})


class WidgetView(SuperAdminOpsView):
    """Authenticated for now; mobile clients will use scoped device tokens later."""
    def get(self, request: Request) -> Response:
```

```
===== services.py =====
"""Composition root for snapshots, dashboard responses, alert state and quiet hours."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from django.core.cache import cache
from django.db import connection
from django.utils import timezone

from console import ops_health

from . import collector
from .health import evaluate
from .models import OpsAlert, OpsConfiguration, OpsSnapshot

SNAPSHOT_CACHE_KEY = "stampn_ops:dashboard"


def _database_metrics() -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        with connection.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity")
            connections = cur.fetchone()[0]
            cur.execute("SELECT pg_database_size(current_database())")
            size = cur.fetchone()[0]
        return {"connected": True, "connections": connections, "size_bytes": size}
    except Exception as exc:
        return {"connected": False, "detail": str(exc)[:200]}


def _business_metrics() -> dict[str, int]:
    # Imported lazily so the module stays importable during migrations.
    from core.models import CustomerCard, Merchant, Redemption, StampLedger
    today = timezone.localdate()
    return {"active_businesses": Merchant.objects.count(),
            "new_businesses": Merchant.objects.filter(created_at__date=today).count(),
            "customers": CustomerCard.objects.filter(created_at__date=today).count(),
            "stamps": StampLedger.objects.filter(created_at__date=today).count(),
            "redemptions": Redemption.objects.filter(created_at__date=today).count(),
            "online_users": 0}  # exact online users requires a future heartbeat, never guessed.


def _alerts(payload: dict[str, Any], thresholds: dict[str, float], penalties: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    now = timezone.now(); open_fingerprints: set[str] = set()
    for penalty in penalties:
        fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(penalty["reason"].encode()).hexdigest()[:40]
        open_fingerprints.add(fingerprint)
        alert, created = OpsAlert.objects.get_or_create(
            fingerprint=fingerprint,
            defaults={"severity": penalty["severity"], "status": "open", "title": "Stampn Ops health alert", "detail": penalty["reason"], "first_seen_at": now, "last_seen_at": now},
        )
        if not created:
            alert.severity = penalty["severity"]; alert.status = "open"; alert.detail = penalty["reason"]
            alert.last_seen_at = now; alert.occurrences += 1; alert.resolved_at = None
            alert.save(update_fields=["severity", "status", "detail", "last_seen_at", "occurrences", "resolved_at", "updated_at"])
    OpsAlert.objects.filter(status="open").exclude(fingerprint__in=open_fingerprints).update(status="resolved", resolved_at=now)


def take_snapshot(*, include_logs: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    config = OpsConfiguration.current()
    host = collector.snapshot(include_logs=include_logs)
    score, status, penalties = evaluate(host, config.thresholds)
    dependencies = ops_health.health_report()
    payload = {**host, "api": dependencies["api"], "database": _database_metrics(),
               "redis": {"connected": dependencies["cache"]["ok"]}, "queues": dependencies["queues"],
               "business": _business_metrics(), "penalties": penalties}
    observed = timezone.now()
    OpsSnapshot.objects.create(observed_at=observed, health_score=score, status=status, payload=payload)
    _alerts(payload, config.thresholds, penalties)
    dashboard = {"observed_at": observed.isoformat(), "health_score": score, "status": status, **payload}
    cache.set(SNAPSHOT_CACHE_KEY, dashboard, 90)
    return dashboard


def dashboard(*, refresh: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cached = None if refresh else cache.get(SNAPSHOT_CACHE_KEY)
    if cached:
        return cached
    latest = OpsSnapshot.objects.order_by("-observed_at").first()
    if latest and latest.observed_at >= timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=2):
        return {"observed_at": latest.observed_at.isoformat(), "health_score": latest.health_score, "status": latest.status, **latest.payload}
    return take_snapshot()


def in_quiet_hours(config: OpsConfiguration, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    if not config.quiet_hours_start or not config.quiet_hours_end:
        return False
    current = (now or timezone.localtime()).time()
    start, end = config.quiet_hours_start, config.quiet_hours_end
    return start <= current < end if start < end else current >= start or current < end

===== health.py =====
"""Deterministic global health scoring and alert candidates."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any


def evaluate(payload: dict[str, Any], thresholds: dict[str, float]) -> tuple[int, str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
    server = payload.get("server", {})
    penalties: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    checks = (("cpu", server.get("cpu_percent"), "cpu_warning", "cpu_critical"),
              ("ram", server.get("ram_percent"), "ram_warning", "ram_critical"),
              ("disk", server.get("disk_percent"), "disk_warning", "disk_critical"))
    score = 100
    for label, value, warning, critical in checks:
        if value is None:
            continue
        if value >= thresholds[critical]:
            score -= 25; penalties.append({"severity": "critical", "reason": f"{label} is {value}%"})
        elif value >= thresholds[warning]:
            score -= 10; penalties.append({"severity": "warning", "reason": f"{label} is {value}%"})
    if not payload.get("available", True):
        score = min(score, 20); penalties.append({"severity": "critical", "reason": "host collector unavailable"})
    docker = payload.get("docker", {})
    if docker.get("stopped", 0) or docker.get("restarting", 0):
        score -= 20; penalties.append({"severity": "critical", "reason": "a platform container is not stable"})
    score = max(0, score)
    return score, "healthy" if score >= 90 else "warning" if score >= 60 else "critical", penalties
```

```
===== collector.py =====
"""Narrow client for the internal host collector. Never falls back to shell."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import httpx
from django.conf import settings


def snapshot(*, include_logs: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    token = getattr(settings, "OPS_COLLECTOR_TOKEN", "")
    if not token:
        return {"available": False, "detail": "collector token is not configured"}
    try:
        response = httpx.get(
            getattr(settings, "OPS_COLLECTOR_URL", "http://ops-collector:9800/v1/snapshot"),
            params={"include_logs": str(include_logs).lower()},
            headers={"X-Ops-Collector-Token": token}, timeout=3.0,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return {"available": True, **response.json()}
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        return {"available": False, "detail": str(exc)[:200]}

===== telegram.py =====
"""Telegram delivery; token decryption is intentionally owned by this module."""
from __future__ import annotations

import httpx
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
from django.conf import settings

from .models import OpsConfiguration


def _token(config: OpsConfiguration) -> str:
    if not config.telegram_bot_token_encrypted:
        return ""
    return Fernet(settings.OPS_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.encode()).decrypt(
        bytes(config.telegram_bot_token_encrypted)).decode()


def send(config: OpsConfiguration, text: str) -> bool:
    token = _token(config)
    if not (config.notifications_enabled and token and config.telegram_chat_id):
        return False
    response = httpx.post(f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{token}/sendMessage",
                          json={"chat_id": config.telegram_chat_id, "text": text[:4000]}, timeout=8.0)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return True

from __future__ import annotations

from celery import shared_task

from .models import OpsConfiguration
from .services import dashboard, in_quiet_hours, take_snapshot
from .telegram import send


@shared_task(queue="default")
def collect_snapshot() -> dict:
    return take_snapshot()


@shared_task(queue="default")
def send_hourly_report() -> bool:
    config = OpsConfiguration.current()
    if not (config.hourly_reports_enabled and not in_quiet_hours(config)):
        return False
    d = dashboard()
    s = d.get("server", {})
    return send(config, "\n".join([f"{'🟢' if d['status'] == 'healthy' else '🟠'} Stampn Production", f"Health Score: {d['health_score']}%", f"CPU: {s.get('cpu_percent', '—')}%", f"RAM: {s.get('ram_percent', '—')}%", f"Disk: {s.get('disk_percent', '—')}%", f"Docker: {d.get('docker', {}).get('running', '—')} running", f"API: {'Healthy' if d.get('api', {}).get('ok') else 'Unavailable'}", f"Version: {d.get('version', '—')}"]))

from __future__ import annotations

from rest_framework import serializers

from .models import OpsConfiguration


class OpsSettingsSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    telegram_bot_token = serializers.CharField(write_only=True, required=False, allow_blank=False)
    telegram_configured = serializers.SerializerMethodField(read_only=True)

    class Meta:
        model = OpsConfiguration
        fields = ["notifications_enabled", "hourly_reports_enabled", "critical_alerts_enabled",
                  "warning_alerts_enabled", "deployment_alerts_enabled", "backup_alerts_enabled",
                  "ssl_alerts_enabled", "telegram_chat_id", "telegram_bot_token",
                  "telegram_configured", "quiet_hours_start", "quiet_hours_end", "thresholds"]

    def get_telegram_configured(self, obj: OpsConfiguration) -> bool:
        return bool(obj.telegram_bot_token_encrypted)

    def validate_thresholds(self, value: dict) -> dict:
        defaults = OpsConfiguration.defaults()
        merged = {**defaults, **value}
        for key, number in merged.items():
            if not isinstance(number, (int, float)) or number < 0:
                raise serializers.ValidationError({key: "Must be a non-negative number."})
        for resource in ("cpu", "ram", "disk"):
            if merged[f"{resource}_warning"] >= merged[f"{resource}_critical"]:
                raise serializers.ValidationError({resource: "Warning must be lower than critical."})
            if merged[f"{resource}_critical"] > 100:
                raise serializers.ValidationError({resource: "Percent cannot exceed 100."})
        return merged
```

```
from __future__ import annotations

import secrets
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Query

from .config import settings
from .monitor import snapshot

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)


def _authorize(token: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="X-Ops-Collector-Token")] = None) -> None:
    if token is None or not secrets.compare_digest(token, settings.token):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="unauthorized")


@app.get("/healthz")
def healthz() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"status": "ok"}


@app.get("/v1/snapshot")
def get_snapshot(
    include_logs: Annotated[bool, Query()] = False,
    _authorized: Annotated[None, Depends(_authorize)] = None,
) -> dict:
    return snapshot(include_logs=include_logs)
```

## 1109 · Claude

I've reviewed both features thoroughly against the real backend. Here's what I found — and it's a mixed picture, which is exactly why checking before merging was the right call.

## stampn-ops — clean, ready to merge

The `console_ops` Django app is genuinely well-built and integrates correctly with the real backend. I verified every cross-module reference:
- `core.models.TimeStampedModel/UUIDModel`, `console.audit.record`, `console.enums.AdminRole`, `console.permissions.AdminAPIView` — all line up, including the `allowed_roles = {SUPER_ADMIN}` gating pattern.
- The critical one: `services.py` calls `console.ops_health.health_report()` expecting `["api"]`, `["cache"]["ok"]`, `["queues"]` — **all three keys exist** in the real function.
- Security posture is sound: Telegram tokens Fernet-encrypted at rest and never returned, collector is a separate FastAPI service with `secrets.compare_digest` token auth and no shell fallback, thresholds validated properly.

Two minor robustness nits (not blockers): `TelegramTestView` can 500 if Telegram rejects the token (uncaught `raise_for_status`), and `WidgetView`'s `responseTime` is always null because the api health check carries no timing. I'd fix the first during merge.

## whatsapp-auth — two real bugs, do not merge as-is

**Showstopper:** in `services.py`, `_check_limits` calls `self._key("hour")` but `_key(self, prefix, phone)` requires the `phone` argument. That's a `TypeError` on **every** `send_otp` call — OTP sending is 100% broken. The tests never call `send_otp`, so nothing caught it.

**Real bug:** `verify_otp` uses `time.monotonic()` to compute OTP expiry across two separate requests. `monotonic()` is per-process — in any multi-worker/multi-host deployment (which prod is), the value stored at send and the value read at verify come from different clock epochs, making the expiry check meaningless (and it re-sets the cache TTL to a garbage value on failed attempts). The cache entry already has a correct 300s TTL, so the fix is to drop the monotonic math entirely.

Both are straightforward fixes. But there's also a **product decision** I can't make for you: WhatsApp was *deliberately removed* three weeks ago (`whatsapp-removal-plan.md`, migration `0013_remove_plan_whatsapp`). That removal was a paid *messaging channel*; this new feature is WhatsApp *OTP login* — different purpose, no table clash — but re-introducing WhatsApp at all is your call, not mine.

<sub>The bug findings are verified against the code; the product concern is me flagging history, not asserting you're wrong to want it back.</sub>

Transport is delegated to\n    ``WhatsAppClient``; this owns the rate limits, the digest comparison, and\n    the account lookup.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, client: WhatsAppClient | None = None):\n        self.client = client or WhatsAppClient()\n\n    def _key(self, prefix: str, phone: str) -> str:\n        return f\"wa_otp:{prefix}:{phone_key(phone)}\"\n\n    def generate_otp(self, phone: str) -> str:\n        return f\"{secrets.randbelow(1_000_000):06d}\"\n\n    def _check_limits(self, phone: str) -> None:\n        if cache.get(self._key(\"cooldown\", phone)):\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Please wait before requesting another code.\")\n        # Same key the send path increments — a per-number hourly ceiling. The\n        # phone argument was the bug that made every send crash before this fix.\n        hourly = self._key(\"hour\", phone)\n        cache.add(hourly, 0, 3600)\n        if int(cache.get(hourly) or 0) >= HOURLY_LIMIT:\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Maximum verification messages reached for this hour.\")\n\n    def send_otp(self, phone: str) -> None:\n        phone = normalize_phone(phone)\n        self._check_limits(phone)\n        otp = self.generate_otp(phone)\n\n        result = self.client.send_template(phone, \"stampn_login\", \"en\", [otp])\n        message_id = (result.get(\"messages\") or [{}])[0].get(\"id\", \"\")\n        WhatsAppMessageLog.objects.create(\n            message_id=message_id, phone_masked=mask_phone(phone), meta_response=result\n        )\n\n        # Expiry is a wall-clock deadline, not a monotonic delta: the code is set\n        # by one worker process and verified by another, and monotonic clocks are\n        # per-process — comparing them across requests is meaningless. The cache\n        # TTL also enforces expiry; this deadline lets a failed attempt re-store\n        # the record without extending its life.\n        cache.set(\n            self._key(\"code\", phone),\n            {\"digest\": otp_digest(phone, otp), \"attempts\": 0, \"expires_at\": time.time() + OTP_TTL},\n            OTP_TTL,\n        )\n        cache.set(self._key(\"cooldown\", phone), True, COOLDOWN_TTL)\n        cache.incr(self._key(\"hour\", phone))\n\n    def verify_otp(self, phone: str, otp: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n        phone = normalize_phone(phone)\n        key = self._key(\"code\", phone)\n        record = cache.get(key)\n        if not record:\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n\n        remaining = int(record.get(\"expires_at\", 0) - time.time())\n        if remaining <= 0:\n            cache.delete(key)\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n        if int(record.get(\"attempts\", 0)) >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:\n            cache.delete(key)\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Too many invalid code attempts.\")\n\n        if not hmac.compare_digest(record[\"digest\"], otp_digest(phone, otp)):\n            record[\"attempts\"] += 1\n            cache.set(key, record, remaining)\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n\n        cache.delete(key)  # a code is single-use, burned on success\n\n        # An OTP proves control of a phone; it does not identify an account. Only\n        # a previously linked, active user gets tokens — an unknown number can\n        # neither create an account nor take one over.\n        identity = WhatsAppIdentity.objects.select_related(\"user\").filter(phone=phone).first()\n        if not identity or not identity.user.is_active:\n            raise OTPInvalid(\"No active account is linked to this phone.\")\n\n        refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(identity.user)\n        return {\"access\": str(refresh.access_token), \"refresh\": str(refresh)}\n\n\ndef link_phone(user, phone: str) -> WhatsAppIdentity:\n    \"\"\"Associate a verified phone with a Django user. Transport is delegated to\n    ``WhatsAppClient``; this owns the rate limits, the digest comparison, and\n    the account lookup.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, client: WhatsAppClient | None = None):\n        self.client = client or WhatsAppClient()\n\n    def _key(self, prefix: str, phone: str) -> str:\n        return f\"wa_otp:{prefix}:{phone_key(phone)}\"\n\n    def generate_otp(self, phone: str) -> str:\n        return f\"{secrets.randbelow(1_000_000):06d}\"\n\n    def _check_limits(self, phone: str) -> None:\n        if cache.get(self._key(\"cooldown\", phone)):\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Please wait before requesting another code.\")\n        # Same key the send path increments — a per-number hourly ceiling. The\n        # missing phone argument here was the bug that crashed every send.\n        hourly = self._key(\"hour\", phone)\n        cache.add(hourly, 0, 3600)\n        if int(cache.get(hourly) or 0) >= HOURLY_LIMIT:\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Maximum verification messages reached for this hour.\")\n\n    def send_otp(self, phone: str) -> None:\n        phone = normalize_phone(phone)\n        self._check_limits(phone)\n        otp = self.generate_otp(phone)\n\n        result = self.client.send_template(phone, \"stampn_login\", \"en\", [otp])\n        message_id = (result.get(\"messages\") or [{}])[0].get(\"id\", \"\")\n        WhatsAppMessageLog.objects.create(\n            message_id=message_id, phone_masked=mask_phone(phone), meta_response=result\n        )\n\n        # Expiry is a wall-clock deadline, not a monotonic delta: a code is set by\n        # one worker process and verified by another, and monotonic clocks are\n        # per-process — comparing them across requests is meaningless. The cache\n        # TTL enforces expiry too; this deadline just lets a failed attempt\n        # re-store the record without extending its life.\n        cache.set(\n            self._key(\"code\", phone),\n            {\"digest\": otp_digest(phone, otp), \"attempts\": 0, \"expires_at\": time.time() + OTP_TTL},\n            OTP_TTL,\n        )\n        cache.set(self._key(\"cooldown\", phone), True, COOLDOWN_TTL)\n        cache.incr(self._key(\"hour\", phone))\n\n    def verify_otp(self, phone: str, otp: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n        phone = normalize_phone(phone)\n        key = self._key(\"code\", phone)\n        record = cache.get(key)\n        if not record:\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n\n        remaining = int(record.get(\"expires_at\", 0) - time.time())\n        if remaining <= 0:\n            cache.delete(key)\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n        if int(record.get(\"attempts\", 0)) >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:\n            cache.delete(key)\n            raise OTPRateLimited(\"Too many invalid code attempts.\")\n\n        if not hmac.compare_digest(record[\"digest\"], otp_digest(phone, otp)):\n            record[\"attempts\"] += 1\n            cache.set(key, record, remaining)\n            raise OTPInvalid()\n\n        cache.delete(key)  # a code is single-use, burned on success\n\n        # An OTP proves control of a phone; it does not identify an account. Only\n        # a previously linked, active user gets tokens — an unknown number can\n        # neither create an account nor take one over.\n        identity = WhatsAppIdentity.objects.select_related(\"user\").filter(phone=phone).first()\n        if not identity or not identity.user.is_active:\n            raise OTPInvalid(\"No active account is linked to this phone.\")\n\n        refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(identity.user)\n        return {\"access\": str(refresh.access_token), \"refresh\": str(refresh)}\n\n\ndef link_phone(user, phone: str) -> WhatsAppIdentity:\n    \"\"\"Associate a verified phone with a Django user. Called from the future\n    signup \/ profile verification flow — the only place a mapping is created.\"\"\"\n    phone = normalize_phone(phone)\n    identity, _ = WhatsAppIdentity.objects.update_or_create(user=user, defaults={\"phone\": phone})\n    return identity\n",

```
=== api.js (base path) ===
import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import api from '../../lib/api'

const root = '/stampn-ops'

export const useOpsDashboard = () =>
  useQuery({ queryKey: ['stampn-ops', 'dashboard'], queryFn: () => api.get(`${root}/dashboard`).then((r) => r.data), refetchInterval: 30_000 })

export const useOpsAlerts = (status = 'open') =>
  useQuery({ queryKey: ['stampn-ops', 'alerts', status], queryFn: () => api.get(`${root}/alerts`, { params: { status } }).then((r) => r.data), refetchInterval: 30_000 })

export const useOpsSettings = () =>
  useQuery({ queryKey: ['stampn-ops', 'settings'], queryFn: () => api.get(`${root}/settings`).then((r) => r.data) })

export const useSaveOpsSettings = () => {
  const qc = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({ mutationFn: (body) => api.patch(`${root}/settings`, body).then((r) => r.data), onSuccess: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['stampn-ops'] }) })
}

export const useTestTelegram = () => useMutation({ mutationFn: () => api.post(`${root}/telegram/test`).then((r) => r.data) })
export const useRefreshOps = () => {
  const qc = useQueryClient()
  return useMutation({ mutationFn: () => api.post(`${root}/refresh`).then((r) => r.data), onSuccess: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['stampn-ops'] }) })
}
```
